q: FB News Feed 这道题里，用户之间的 follow 关系被简化成什么模型？
q_en: In the FB News Feed problem, what model is the user follow relationship simplified to?
options: 双向好友关系，必须两边都主动发出请求并互相确认后才成立
单向 follow：A 关注 B，不需要 B 同意
群组成员关系，需要管理员审批才能加入
只有互相关注的双方才能看到对方发的帖子
options_en: A bidirectional friend relationship that exists only after both sides actively send a request and confirm each other.
A one-way follow: A follows B without B agreeing.
A group-membership relationship that needs admin approval before joining.
Posts are visible only when both sides mutually follow each other.
why: 早期 Facebook 以双向好友为主，但本题明确简化为单向 follow：关注是一条有方向的边，不需要对方同意。
why_en: This problem deliberately simplifies to a one-way follow edge instead of Facebook's original bidirectional friend model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单向的关注关系，A 关注 B 不需要 B 同意。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follow is a one-directional relationship where A follows B without B's consent.

optionExplanations: 这套是老版 Facebook 的双向好友模型，双方都得确认，和本题设定不同。
对：本题把关注建模成 A→B 的单向边，A 说了算，不用 B 同意。
群组成员靠管理员审批加入，是另一套产品逻辑，题目没引入这个概念。
『必须互关才能看见』是虚构的附加规则，本题单向关注就能看到对方帖子。
optionExplanations_en: That's the old bidirectional Facebook friend model where both sides confirm, which isn't this problem's setup.
Correct: this problem models a follow as a one-way A-to-B edge that A alone creates, no approval from B needed.
Group membership requiring admin approval is a different product concept this problem never introduces.
Requiring mutual follow to see posts is an invented rule; here a one-way follow already unlocks visibility.
scenario: 设计 FB News Feed：名人账号有千万粉丝，不可能逐个确认，关系模型必须支持这种不对称。
scenario_en: We are designing FB News Feed, where a celebrity has tens of millions of followers and can never approve each one, so the relationship model has to handle that asymmetry.

q: News Feed 的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which features are in scope for the News Feed MVP? (Select all that apply.)
scenario: 面试官只给了一句话：设计 Facebook 的 News Feed。你要先圈定这道题的功能范围。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says: design Facebook News Feed. First, define the functional scope.
options: 用户能创建帖子
用户能关注（follow）他人
用户能按时间倒序查看关注对象的 feed，并能翻页
用户能点赞和评论帖子
帖子支持私密/受限可见性
options_en: Users can create posts.
Users can follow other people.
Users can view a reverse-chronological feed from who they follow, with pagination.
Users can like and comment on posts.
Posts support private or restricted visibility.
why: 核心需求只有三类：发帖、关注、按时间倒序翻页看 feed。点赞评论和可见性控制被明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The core scope is only posting, following, and paging a reverse-chronological feed; likes, comments, and visibility rules are explicitly out of scope.
optionExplanations: 发帖是本题的主写路径，一旦选中就决定了要设计 Post API 和帖子表。
关注是社交图谱的基础边，选中它才谈得上后面的写扇出、读扇出问题。
倒序+翻页是读侧的硬性功能点，直接决定 Feed Service 和游标设计。
点赞评论会带来额外的计数和实体，本题明确把它划出范围，省下这块复杂度。
可见性控制要接一层权限过滤，题目里没这个需求，加了反而分散精力。
optionExplanations_en: Posting is the core write path here, and picking it means designing the Post API and a posts table.
Follow is the basic edge of the social graph, and without it there's no fan-out problem to even discuss.
Reverse-chronological paging is a hard read-side requirement that shapes the Feed Service and its cursor.
Likes and comments would add extra entities and counters that this problem deliberately keeps out of scope.
Visibility control needs a permission-filtering layer this problem never asks for, so adding it just adds noise.

scenario: 面试官只给了一句话：设计 Facebook 的 News Feed。你量化出：最多 1 分钟陈旧、发帖和刷 feed 都要 500ms 内返回、约 20 亿用户。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says: design Facebook News Feed. You quantify the NFRs as up to one minute of staleness, post/feed responses under 500ms, and about two billion users.
q: 这些非功能数字最支持哪些设计判断？
q_en: Which design decisions do these non-functional numbers support?
text: 1 分钟陈旧窗口支持{{异步写扇出}}；500ms 延迟目标排除{{读时大扇出}}；20 亿用户要求认真做{{存储与分区}}。
why: 这四个数字直接驱动后面的架构决策：1 分钟陈旧窗口允许异步写扇出，500ms 排除了读时大扇出，20 亿用户决定了存储与分区策略。
why_en: These four numbers directly drive the architecture: the one-minute window enables async fan-out, 500ms rules out big read-time fan-out, and 2 billion users shapes storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在故障时仍能响应请求的能力，这里被优先于强一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability is the system's ability to keep responding during failures; here it is prioritized over strong consistency.

scenario: 社交 feed：用户晚 1 分钟看到新帖几乎无感知，但 app 打不开会直接流失用户。
scenario_en: In a social feed, a post appearing one minute late is barely noticed, but an unavailable app loses users.
q: 在一致性与可用性之间应该怎么选？
q_en: For this social feed, how should we choose between consistency and availability?
options: 优先可用性，接受最终一致——帖子可以短暂陈旧
优先强一致，宁可直接拒绝请求或返回错误，也绝不给出旧数据
读写都做线性一致
牺牲分区容忍来换两者兼得
options_en: Favor availability and accept eventual consistency; posts can be briefly stale.
Favor strong consistency, rejecting the request or returning an error rather than ever serving stale data.
Make both reads and writes linearizable.
Give up partition tolerance to get both at once.
why: feed 陈旧一分钟没人在乎，打不开才是灾难，所以选可用性 + 最终一致。这个选择随后解锁异步扇出、缓存等一整套手段。
why_en: A one-minute-stale feed goes unnoticed but a down app does not, so this system favors availability with eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 支付、库存、抢票这类返回旧数据会造成真实损失的系统，必须反过来优先强一致。
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 一致性

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内不同副本可能不一致，但最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may briefly disagree after a write but converge to the same value over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强一致性模型，所有读写看起来像按一个全局顺序发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strongest consistency model, where all reads and writes appear to happen in one global order.

optionExplanations: 对：feed 陈旧一分钟没人有感，但打不开 app 用户立刻流失，所以优先可用性。
支付、抢票这类『错一次就是真损失』的场景才该反过来选它，本题不是。
全局线性一致代价极高，本题读写量级下没必要为一分钟的陈旧买这个单。
分布式系统跨机器部署，网络分区迟早发生，放弃分区容忍不是真实选项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: a feed being a minute stale goes unnoticed, but a down app loses users instantly, so this system favors availability.
Strong consistency is the right call when stale reads cause real loss, like payments or ticket holds, not this feed.
Fully linearizable reads and writes cost far more than this feed's tolerance for one-minute staleness justifies.
A distributed system spread across machines will hit network partitions eventually, so giving that up isn't realistic.

q: 为什么非功能需求要写上具体数字，而不是只说『要快、要大』？
q_en: Why should non-functional requirements use concrete numbers instead of just saying 'fast' and 'large'?
options: 面试评分表硬性要求写数字
数字决定架构，量级不同设计不同
写数字显得更专业
方便直接换算需要多少台服务器
options_en: Interview rubrics rigidly require numbers.
Numbers decide the architecture: single-digit-millisecond and sub-second latency need very different designs.
Writing numbers just looks more professional.
It lets you directly convert to a server headcount.
why: 量化才能做取舍：要求个位毫秒的系统和允许一秒返回的系统，架构会截然不同，数字是后续每个决策的依据。
why_en: Quantifying requirements is what enables real tradeoffs, since a single-digit-millisecond system and a one-second system need very different architectures.
optionExplanations: 没有固定评分表逼你写数字，这是把动机想歪了。
对：个位毫秒和亚秒级系统的架构完全不同，数字才是后面每个决策的依据。
写数字不是为了显得专业，是为了让后面的取舍有据可依。
算服务器数只是数字的一个下游用途，不是『要写数字』这件事本身的原因。
optionExplanations_en: There's no fixed rubric forcing numbers into the write-up — that misreads the motivation.
Correct: single-digit-millisecond and sub-second systems need very different architectures, and the numbers drive every later decision.
Writing numbers isn't about looking professional, it's about giving later tradeoffs something concrete to point to.
Converting to a server headcount is just one downstream use of the numbers, not the reason to quantify in the first place.
scenario: 为 News Feed 写非功能需求：接下来要据此决定是否预计算 feed、缓存多久，写完立刻选型。
scenario_en: We're writing the non-functional requirements for News Feed, and the very next step is deciding whether to precompute feeds and how long to cache.

q: News Feed 设计里，架构上公认最难、最值得预留时间深挖的部分是？
q_en: In the News Feed design, which part deserves the most deep-dive time?
options: 用户认证与鉴权
帖子富文本的存储格式
海量关注/粉丝的扇出问题
数据库备份与恢复
options_en: User authentication and authorization.
The storage format for rich-text posts.
Fan-out: what happens when a user follows huge numbers of accounts, or an account has huge numbers of followers.
Database backup and recovery.
why: 难点是扇出：关注很多人让读扇出爆炸，被很多人关注让写扇出爆炸。基础需求要快速铺完，把时间省给这里。
why_en: The hard part is fan-out, since following many accounts explodes read fan-out and having many followers explodes write fan-out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求或写入在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求或写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request or write gets amplified into many downstream requests or writes.

optionExplanations: 身份认证在这类题里通常一句带过，不是本题要深挖的难点。
帖子内容结构留空对象就够，细节不是这道题的价值所在。
对：关注很多人读扇出炸，被很多人关注写扇出炸，这才是真正难啃的部分。
备份恢复属于运维话题，和这道设计题的核心矛盾没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Authentication is usually a one-line mention in this kind of problem, not the part worth deep-diving.
Rich-text storage can stay an empty placeholder object; the details aren't where this problem's value is.
Correct: following many accounts explodes read fan-out, and having many followers explodes write fan-out — that's the real hard part.
Backup and recovery is an ops concern, unrelated to this design problem's central tension.
scenario: 45 分钟面试设计 News Feed：用户平均关注数百人、名人有千万粉丝，时间只够深挖一处。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute News Feed interview, users follow hundreds of accounts and celebrities have millions of followers, so there's only time to go deep on one area.

q: News Feed 系统的核心实体有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which entities are core to the News Feed system? (Select all that apply.)
options: User：系统中的用户
Follow：用户之间的单向链接，显式建成实体
Post：用户发布的帖子，出现在粉丝的 feed 里
Comment：帖子下的评论
Session：登录会话
options_en: User: a user of the system.
Follow: a one-directional link between users, modeled as its own entity.
Post: content a user publishes, shown in followers' feeds.
Comment: a comment under a post.
Session: a login session.
why: 核心实体只有三个：User、Follow、Post。把 Follow 显式建成实体而不是 User 的属性，是后面所有扇出讨论的基础。
why_en: There are only three core entities: User, Follow, and Post, and modeling Follow as its own entity is the foundation for every fan-out discussion later.
optionExplanations: User 是发帖者也是读者，所有请求的鉴权都要围着它转。
把 Follow 单独设计成实体，才能后续给写扇出、读扇出建索引和查询路径。
Post 是 feed 内容的来源，缓存和存储设计都得围着它展开。
评论会引入新的计数和实体，本题先不建模，省下这块复杂度。
登录会话属于认证细节，不参与决定 feed 的数据模型，不用建它。
optionExplanations_en: User is both author and reader, so every request's authorization revolves around it.
Giving Follow its own entity gives every later fan-out design something concrete, like indexes and queries, to attach to.
Post is where feed content comes from, so caching and storage design both center on it.
Comments would introduce new counters and entities that this problem leaves unmodeled to keep scope tight.
A login session is an auth detail that plays no role in shaping the feed's data model, so it doesn't need modeling.
scenario: 为 News Feed 建核心实体：产品只要发帖、关注、倒序 feed，且要支撑按粉丝反查的扇出。
scenario_en: We are modeling core entities for News Feed: only posting, following, and a reverse-chronological feed, and it must support looking up followers for fan-out.

scenario: 第一个功能：发帖。内容可能是富文本或其他结构化数据，且发帖人身份不能被客户端伪造。
scenario_en: The first feature is post creation. Content may be rich or structured, and the author identity must not be spoofable by the client.
q: 哪个 API 设计最合适？
q_en: Which post-creation API design is the best fit?
options: GET /posts?content=... 把帖子内容当查询参数传，不走请求体
POST /posts，body 只放 content，身份来自 JWT，返回 postId
POST /posts，body 里除 content 外还显式带一个 userId 字段指明发帖人是谁
PUT /posts，用覆盖语义直接替换该用户当前最新的一条帖子
options_en: GET /posts?content=... treats the post content as a query parameter instead of a body.
POST /posts with only a content object in the body; identity comes from the JWT, response returns postId.
POST /posts with, besides the content object, an explicit userId field in the body naming who the author is.
PUT /posts, using overwrite semantics to directly replace the user's current latest post.
why: POST /posts 只带 content：内容留成对象以兼容富媒体，发帖人从认证头（JWT）取——放 body 里的 userId 客户端可以伪造。
why_en: POST /posts carries only a content object so it can hold rich media, while the author identity comes from the JWT header instead of a spoofable body field.
whenOtherWins: 如果客户端要离线生成、断网重试并保证幂等，PUT + 客户端生成的 postId 也是合理设计。
tradeoff: 身份来自可信请求头 vs 客户端自报身份

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把用户身份编码进请求头的签名令牌格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity, carried in the request header.

optionExplanations: GET 语义是取数据不是写数据，用查询参数传内容也会撞上 URL 长度限制。
对：body 只放 content 对象方便日后塞富媒体，身份从 JWT 取，客户端伪造不了。
body 里的 userId 是客户端自己填的，谁都能改成别人的 ID，等于允许冒名发帖。
PUT 覆盖语义意味着每次发帖会顶掉上一条，这不是『新增一条帖子』该有的语义。
optionExplanations_en: GET is for fetching, not writing, and cramming content into a query string also runs into URL length limits.
Correct: a body holding only content leaves room for rich media, while identity comes from the JWT, which a client can't spoof.
A userId field in the body is client-supplied, so anyone could edit it to impersonate another author.
PUT's overwrite semantics would replace the previous post on every call, which isn't what 'create a new post' should mean.

q: 关注接口为什么选 PUT /users/[id]/follow 而不是 POST？
q_en: Why use PUT /users/[id]/follow instead of POST for the follow endpoint?
options: PUT 幂等，重复点击不报错
PUT 传输速度更快
POST 不支持路径参数
PUT 可以跳过网关鉴权
options_en: PUT is idempotent: double-clicking follow twice leaves the same result without an error.
PUT transmits faster.
POST doesn't support path parameters.
PUT can skip gateway authentication.
why: 关注是二元状态，用 PUT 保证幂等，重复点击不会出错；取消关注（超纲）可用同一路径的 DELETE。
why_en: Following is a binary state, so PUT keeps it idempotent and repeated clicks never error out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is repeated.

optionExplanations: 对：关注是个二元状态，PUT 幂等，重复点两次结果一样，不会报错。
PUT 和 POST 在传输速度上没有本质差别，这不是选它的真正理由。
POST 完全可以带路径参数，这个说法本身就不成立。
PUT 和 POST 一样要过网关鉴权，没有谁能跳过这一层。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: following is a binary state, and PUT is idempotent, so clicking follow twice still lands in the same result with no error.
PUT and POST have no meaningful difference in transmission speed, so that isn't the real reason.
POST can absolutely take path parameters, so that claim is just false.
PUT goes through the same gateway auth as POST; neither method gets a free pass.
scenario: News Feed 关注接口：移动端弱网会自动重试，用户也会连点，同一请求可能到达多次。
scenario_en: For the News Feed follow endpoint, flaky mobile networks retry and users double-tap, so the same request can arrive several times.

q: PUT /users/[id]/follow 中，『谁在关注谁』是如何确定的？
q_en: In PUT /users/[id]/follow, how do we know who follows whom?
options: body 里带 followerId 和 followeeId 两个字段
都放在 query string 里
被关注者来自 JWT，关注者是路径里的 [id]
关注者来自请求头的 JWT，被关注者是路径里的 [id]
options_en: Two body fields, followerId and followeeId.
Both values are passed in the query string.
The followee comes from the JWT, the follower is the path [id].
The follower comes from the JWT header, the followee is the path [id].
why: 发起关注的一定是当前认证用户（JWT 里的身份），路径参数 [id] 是被关注的人；身份永远不信任客户端传的 body。
why_en: The follower is always the authenticated caller from the JWT, while the path parameter [id] names who gets followed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把用户身份编码进请求头的签名令牌格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity, carried in the request header.

optionExplanations: 让客户端在 body 里自报双方身份，等于允许伪造成别人去关注。
把双方身份塞进 URL 参数，一样绕不开『客户端可以乱填』的问题。
把路径参数和 JWT 的角色对调了，被关注者才该来自路径，不是反过来。
对：关注者永远是当前登录用户（JWT），路径里的 [id] 才是被关注对象。
optionExplanations_en: Letting the client self-declare both identities in the body means anyone could forge being someone else's follower.
Putting both identities into URL parameters still doesn't escape the problem of a client filling in anything it wants.
This swaps the roles: the path parameter should name the followee, not the follower.
Correct: the follower is always the currently authenticated user from the JWT, and the path [id] names who gets followed.
scenario: News Feed 关注接口开在公网，客户端完全不可信；请求经网关校验 JWT 后到达服务。
scenario_en: The News Feed follow endpoint is public and the client is untrusted; requests reach the service after the gateway validates a JWT.

scenario: feed 按时间从新到旧返回，客户端不断上滑加载更旧内容（无限滚动）。
scenario_en: The feed returns newest-to-oldest posts, and the client keeps scrolling upward to load older content.
q: 哪个接口设计最合适？
q_en: Which feed pagination API design is the best fit?
options: GET /feed?page=3&pageSize=20，靠整数页码偏移量 offset 做分页
GET /feed 一次性返回全部 feed 内容
GET /feed?pageSize={n}&cursor={timestamp}
POST /feed，body 传回全部已看过的 postId 列表
options_en: GET /feed?page=3&pageSize=20, offset pagination using an integer page offset.
GET /feed returning the entire feed content at once.
GET /feed?pageSize={n}&cursor={timestamp}, with nextCursor in the response.
POST /feed with a body listing every postId already seen.
why: 已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳一个值就完整描述进度，每页返回比它更旧的 N 条，比 offset 更稳定（新帖插入不会错位）。
why_en: A single timestamp cursor fully describes how far the user has scrolled, and it stays stable even when new posts are inserted, unlike offset pagination.
whenOtherWins: 数据量小且几乎不变的列表（后台管理页）用 offset/limit 更省事。
tradeoff: 游标分页的稳定性 vs offset 分页的简单直观

termDefinitions.meaning: 翻页用的标记，记录用户已看到的位置，用来取下一页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor is a pagination marker recording how far a user has scrolled, used to fetch the next page.

optionExplanations: offset 分页在数据量小且几乎不变的后台页面很好用，但 feed 一直插入新帖会导致错位。
一次性吐出全部 feed，量级上完全撑不住无限滚动这种持续增长的列表。
对：游标只需要一个时间戳，服务端不用存任何会话状态，翻页天然幂等。
让客户端携带全部已见 postId，列表只会越滚越长，纯粹的浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Offset pagination is fine for small, mostly-static admin lists, but new posts keep shifting the offsets here.
Dumping the entire feed in one response can't scale to an endlessly growing, infinitely scrolling list.
Correct: the cursor is just one timestamp, so the server keeps zero session state and paging stays naturally idempotent.
Having the client carry every seen postId means that list only grows and grows, which is pure waste.

q: feed 接口里的 cursor 具体代表什么？
q_en: What does the cursor in the feed API represent?
options: 当前用户的 ID
服务端分配的页码
服务端随机生成的一个会话令牌字符串
用户已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳
options_en: The current user's ID.
A page number assigned by the server.
A random session token string generated by the server.
The timestamp of the oldest post the user has already seen.
why: 用户从新往旧看，一个时间戳就能标记『看到哪了』，天然有序、无需服务端存状态。
why_en: Since users scroll from newest to oldest, a single timestamp marks exactly how far they've read, with no server-side state needed.
optionExplanations: 把 cursor 和用户身份混为一谈了，两者是完全不同的字段。
cursor 不是传统页码，它不依赖『第几页』这种固定切分。
cursor 也不是认证令牌，它跟身份验证没有关系。
对：cursor 就是用户已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳，天然有序不用服务端存状态。
optionExplanations_en: That conflates the cursor with the user's identity, which is a completely separate field.
The cursor isn't a classic page number; it doesn't depend on a fixed 'page N' slicing.
The cursor also isn't an auth token — it has nothing to do with authentication.
Correct: the cursor is exactly the timestamp of the oldest post the user has already seen, naturally ordered with no server state.
scenario: News Feed 倒序翻页每页 20 条，服务端要无状态可水平扩容，不为用户保存浏览进度。
scenario_en: News Feed pages 20 posts at a time in reverse-chronological order, and the service must stay stateless so it can scale horizontally.

q: 定义 API 时把帖子的 content 保持为空对象、暂不展开结构，动机是什么？
q_en: Why keep the post content field as an empty object instead of modeling its structure now?
options: 留扩展位，也把时间留给核心难点
帖子内容其实存在另一个系统里
JSON 不允许深层嵌套
内容结构由前端决定，后端无权定义
options_en: It leaves room for structured rich content while saving interview time for higher-value topics.
Post content is actually stored in a separate system.
JSON doesn't allow deeply nested structures.
Content structure is decided by the frontend, and the backend has no say.
why: content 留成对象可以日后装任何富内容；不深挖 Post 结构也是刻意的时间管理，把精力留给扇出这类核心难点。
why_en: Leaving content as an object keeps room for any future rich content, and skipping its details is a deliberate way to save time for the harder fan-out problems.
optionExplanations: 对：留成空对象既给富内容留了扩展位，也是刻意把时间省给扇出这类真正难点。
帖子内容并没有真的存在另一个系统里，这是编出来的理由。
JSON 完全支持深层嵌套，这个限制根本不存在。
后端当然有权定义内容结构，把决定权全推给前端是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: leaving it an empty object saves room for rich content later and deliberately saves interview time for the real hard part, fan-out.
Post content isn't actually stored in some other system — that's a made-up explanation.
JSON fully supports deep nesting, so that limitation simply doesn't exist.
The backend absolutely has a say in content structure; handing that entirely to the frontend is wrong.
scenario: 45 分钟面试里定 News Feed API：核心难点是扇出，而帖子的富文本格式以后还会变。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute News Feed interview the hard part is fan-out, and the post's rich-content format will keep changing later.

scenario: 发帖服务只往数据库写数据、本机不保存任何状态；流量增长时希望直接加机器就能扩容。
scenario_en: The post service only writes to the database and keeps no local state, so traffic growth should be handled by adding more machines.
q: 发帖链路的高层设计应该是？
q_en: What should the high-level post creation path look like?
options: 一台高配服务器垂直扩容
把会话状态放进各台服务器的内存，再用粘性路由绑定用户
无状态 Post Service，加机器即扩容
先拆成几十个微服务再谈扩容
options_en: One beefier server, scaled vertically.
Keep session state in each server's own memory and pin users to it with sticky routing.
API gateway plus load balancer in front of a stateless, horizontally scaled Post Service.
Split into dozens of microservices before even discussing scaling.
why: 每台主机无状态（只写库），所以水平扩展极其简单：网关/负载均衡后面随意加机器。
why_en: Because every host is stateless and only writes to the database, horizontal scaling is as simple as adding more machines behind the gateway and load balancer.
whenOtherWins: 若服务必须维护本机状态（长连接、会话），要先做状态外置或粘性会话才能水平扩。
tradeoff: 无状态水平扩展 vs 有状态但可能更快的本地路径

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务实例不在本机保存请求间的状态，因此可以随意加减实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless service keeps no per-request state on the instance, so instances can be added or removed freely.

optionExplanations: 单机垂直扩容总会撞到硬件天花板，撑不住持续增长的流量。
把会话状态放进内存需要粘性路由，这套系统压根没有会话状态要保留。
对：Post Service 只写库、本机不留状态，网关/负载均衡后面加机器就能扩。
在流量和团队都还小的阶段就先拆几十个微服务，只会平白增加运维负担。
optionExplanations_en: Vertically scaling one bigger box always hits a hardware ceiling that can't keep up with steady growth.
Keeping session state in memory needs sticky routing, but this service has no session state to keep in the first place.
Correct: since Post Service only writes to the database and holds no local state, scaling is just adding machines behind the gateway and load balancer.
Splitting into dozens of microservices before traffic or the team justify it just adds operational overhead for nothing.

scenario: 存帖子：按 ID 写入/读取的简单键值访问模式，20 亿用户规模，需要能预置极高吞吐。
scenario_en: Posts are simple key-value writes and reads by ID at a 2-billion-user scale, with very high provisioned throughput.
q: 文中选择的存储及理由是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits posts, and why?
options: DynamoDB：负载均匀时吞吐很高
单实例 Postgres，靠索引硬撑
Neo4j，社交产品默认用图数据库
全内存数据库，所有帖子放 RAM
options_en: DynamoDB: simple and horizontally scalable, delivering very high throughput as long as load is spread evenly across partitions.
A single Postgres instance, pushed hard with indexes.
Neo4j, on the assumption social products default to a graph database.
An all-in-memory database, keeping every post in RAM.
why: 访问模式是简单 KV（按 ID 存取），DynamoDB 简单又能水平扩到极高吞吐——前提是负载在分区间均匀。
why_en: Since access is a simple by-ID key-value pattern, DynamoDB scales to very high throughput as long as load stays even across partitions.
whenOtherWins: 需要复杂关系查询或多表事务时，关系型数据库更合适。
tradeoff: 水平扩展的简单 KV vs 复杂关系查询能力

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 key-value 数据库，靠分区实现水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value database that scales horizontally by partitioning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款专用的图数据库，擅长多跳关系遍历。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a purpose-built graph database good at multi-hop relationship traversal.

optionExplanations: 对：按 ID 存取是简单 KV 模式，DynamoDB 分区均匀时能水平扩到极高吞吐。
单机 Postgres 靠索引硬撑，20 亿用户规模下垂直扩容迟早撞墙。
Neo4j 的强项是图遍历，本题只是按 ID 存取帖子，用不上这层能力。
全内存存全部帖子在这个规模下内存成本高到不现实，还没解决持久化。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: since access is a simple by-ID key-value pattern, DynamoDB scales horizontally to very high throughput once load is even.
A single Postgres instance leaning on indexes will eventually hit a vertical ceiling at 2 billion users.
Neo4j's strength is graph traversal, and this problem only needs by-ID post access, so that power goes unused.
Keeping every post in RAM at this scale means unrealistic memory cost, and it still doesn't solve durability.

scenario: follow 是多对多关系，本题只需三种简单查询：A 是否关注 B、A 关注了谁、谁关注 A，不做多跳遍历。
scenario_en: Follow is a many-to-many relationship, but this problem only needs three simple queries: does A follow B, who does A follow, and who follows A.
q: 关系数据用什么存？
q_en: What should store follow relationships?
options: Neo4j 专用图数据库
triple store 三元组存储
文档数据库，用嵌套数组存粉丝列表
普通 KV 表自己把图建模出来
options_en: A dedicated graph database like Neo4j.
A triple store.
A document database, storing follower lists as nested arrays.
A plain key-value table that models the graph itself.
why: 图数据库的价值在遍历和图推导，这题查询固定又简单，KV 表两个键就能表达，还避开了给自己挖『如何扩展图库』的坑。
why_en: Graph databases earn their keep on traversal, but this problem's queries are fixed and simple enough that a two-key KV table covers them without adding a new system to scale.
whenOtherWins: 要做朋友的朋友、图 embedding 这类多跳遍历时，专用图数据库才真正值得引入。
tradeoff: 简单 KV 建模 vs 专用图数据库的遍历能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款专用的图数据库，擅长多跳关系遍历。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a purpose-built graph database good at multi-hop relationship traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以（主体, 谓词, 客体）三元组存储关系数据的图数据库形态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A triple store models relationships as subject-predicate-object triples.

optionExplanations: 图数据库的价值在多跳遍历，本题只有三种固定的简单查询，用不上这层能力。
三元组存储也是为图推导设计的，同样是为本题不需要的能力多付一份代价。
把粉丝列表塞进嵌套数组，单个热门账号的数组会变得又大又难更新。
对：两个键就能表达『谁关注谁』，查询固定又简单，还省掉运维一个新系统。
optionExplanations_en: A graph database earns its keep on multi-hop traversal, but this problem only needs three fixed, simple lookups.
A triple store is likewise built for graph inference, paying for capability this problem never asked for.
Stuffing follower lists into nested arrays makes a popular account's array huge and awkward to update.
Correct: two keys fully express 'who follows whom' for these fixed, simple queries, without standing up a new system to operate.

q: 在『多跳遍历/图推导』这个维度上，专用图数据库和自建 KV 关系表的对比是？
q_en: How do a graph database and a custom KV relationship table compare for multi-hop traversal?
options: 两者能力其实一样，差别只在价格
KV 表反而更擅长做多跳遍历
图数据库擅长跨节点步进；KV 表只适合固定单跳查询
图数据库只是厂商包装出来的营销概念，和 KV 表没有真实能力差异
options_en: Both actually have the same capability, differing only in price.
The KV table is actually the one better at multi-hop traversal.
Graph databases excel at stepping across nodes; a KV table only fits fixed single-hop queries.
Graph databases are just vendor marketing, with no real capability difference from a KV table.
why: 图数据库的强项是需要在节点间反复步进的查询——朋友的朋友、图 embedding；固定的单跳查询，KV 表就够，还省掉运维一个新系统。
why_en: Graph databases shine at queries that hop repeatedly between nodes, while a fixed single-hop query is fully covered by a KV table without adding a new system.
tradeoff: 多跳遍历能力 vs 运维简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询需要在图上连续跳过多个节点，比如朋友的朋友。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-hop traversal means a query must step across several graph nodes in sequence, like friends of friends.

optionExplanations: 两者的遍历能力其实差得很远，说『一样只差价格』是没有的事。
这把两者的强项说反了，KV 表恰恰不擅长多跳。
对：图数据库擅长跨节点反复步进，KV 表只吃得下固定的单跳查询。
图数据库在多跳查询上的优势是真实的工程能力差异，不是营销话术。
optionExplanations_en: Their traversal capability actually differs a lot; 'same capability, just price' isn't true.
This reverses the actual strengths — a KV table is specifically weak at multi-hop traversal.
Correct: graph databases excel at stepping repeatedly across nodes, while a KV table only handles fixed single-hop queries.
A graph database's edge on multi-hop queries is a real engineering difference, not marketing spin.
scenario: News Feed 只查『我关注谁 / 谁关注我』这类单跳关系，团队也没人专职运维新数据库。
scenario_en: News Feed only needs single-hop lookups like who I follow and who follows me, and nobody on the team can operate an extra database.

scenario: 在 DynamoDB 建 Follow 表，要求：① 点查『A 是否关注 B』；② range 查『A 关注的所有人』。
scenario_en: Build a DynamoDB Follow table that can point-check whether A follows B and range-query everyone A follows.
q: 主键应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the Follow table primary key be designed?
options: PK = userFollowing，SK = userFollowed
PK = userFollowed，SK = userFollowing
PK = 随机 followId，无 SK
把整份关注列表序列化成一个大 JSON 存成单行
options_en: Partition key = userFollowing, sort key = userFollowed.
Partition key = userFollowed, sort key = userFollowing.
Partition key = a random followId, with no sort key.
Serialize the whole follow list into one giant JSON row.
codeSample:
Table: Follow
  Partition key: userFollowing
  Sort key:      userFollowed

-- A follows B?   get(PK=A, SK=B)
-- who does A follow?  query(PK=A)
why: 分区键 userFollowing + 排序键 userFollowed：两键齐给就是点查关系，只给分区键就是 range 查 A 的全部关注对象。
why_en: Partitioning by userFollowing and sorting by userFollowed lets you point-query the relationship with both keys, or range-query everyone A follows with just the partition key.
whenOtherWins: 若最高频查询是『谁关注了我』，就该把 userFollowed 当分区键——这正是反向 GSI 补上的方向。
tradeoff: 服务『我关注了谁』 vs 服务『谁关注我』

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定数据落在哪个物理分区的键，同分区键的数据支持排序键的 range 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which physical partition data lands on; items sharing a partition key can be range-queried by sort key.

optionExplanations: 对：分区键是关注者、排序键是被关注者，两键齐给能点查，只给分区键能 range 查全部关注对象。
把分区键和排序键的角色对调了，这样反而先服务不了『A 关注了谁』这个高频查询。
随机键丢掉了排序能力，连 range 查询这个基本需求都满足不了。
把整份关注列表压进一行大 JSON，单行大小和并发写入都会先出问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: partitioning by follower and sorting by followee supports a point lookup with both keys, or a range query for everyone A follows with just the partition key.
Swapping which field is the partition key breaks the high-frequency 'who does A follow' query first.
A random key throws away sort capability, so it can't even satisfy a basic range query.
Packing the whole follow list into one giant JSON row runs into row-size and concurrent-write problems first.

q: Follow 表上那个 GSI（全局二级索引）是用来做什么的？
q_en: What is the GSI on the Follow table used for?
options: 提升写入吞吐
把关注关系里的帖子按创建时间排序
防止重复关注
反转键序，支持查粉丝列表
options_en: Boosting write throughput.
Sorting the follow relationship's posts by creation time.
Preventing duplicate follows.
Reversing the key order to support a range query for 'all followers of a user'.
why: 主表只能按『我关注了谁』查；把键反过来建 GSI，才能按 userFollowed 一次 range 查询拉出全部粉丝——写扇出时 worker 就靠它。
why_en: The base table only answers 'who I follow', so the GSI reverses the keys to range-query all of a user's followers, which is exactly what fan-out workers rely on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引，支持另一种查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key that supports another query pattern.

optionExplanations: GSI 的作用和写入吞吐没关系，这是张冠李戴。
帖子排序另有它法，跟这张 Follow 表的索引不是一回事。
防重复关注要靠主键约束，不是这个 GSI 的职责。
对：主表只能查『我关注了谁』，反转键序建 GSI 才能一次 range 查出全部粉丝。
optionExplanations_en: The GSI's role has nothing to do with write throughput — that's misattributing it.
Post ordering is handled elsewhere; it's unrelated to this Follow-table index.
Preventing duplicate follows is a primary-key constraint's job, not this GSI's.
Correct: the base table only answers 'who do I follow', so reversing the keys in a GSI lets one range query pull all of a user's followers.
scenario: 写扇出 worker 收到一条新帖，要立刻拿到作者的全部粉丝列表才能去更新他们的 feed。
scenario_en: A fan-out worker picks up a new post and must immediately pull the full follower list of the author to update their feeds.

q: Follow 表 + 反向 GSI 一共支持哪些查询？（多选）
q_en: Which queries are supported by the Follow table plus the reverse GSI? (Select all that apply.)
options: PK+SK 点查：判断 A 是否关注了 B
主表 PK range 查询：A 关注的所有人
GSI PK range 查询：关注 A 的所有人
一条查询直接拿到『朋友的朋友』
options_en: PK+SK point lookup: is A following B?
Base-table PK range query: everyone A follows.
GSI PK range query: everyone who follows A.
A single query that returns 'friends of friends' directly.
why: 三种查询正好覆盖全部功能需求：关系点查、正向列表、反向列表。多跳遍历不支持——那是图数据库的领域。
why_en: These three queries cover the full functional scope: relationship lookup, forward list, and reverse list, but multi-hop traversal is left to graph databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引，支持另一种查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key that supports another query pattern.

optionExplanations: 两键齐给就是点查，直接判断 A 是否已经关注了 B。
只给主表分区键就是 range 查询，拉出 A 关注的全部对象。
反向 GSI 的分区键 range 查询，专门拉出关注 A 的全部粉丝，写扇出靠它。
朋友的朋友要连续跳两次关系，这张两键 KV 表天生做不到，得靠图数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Point lookup with both keys directly answers whether A already follows B.
A range query on just the base table's partition key pulls everyone A follows.
A range query on the reverse GSI's partition key pulls everyone who follows A, exactly what write fan-out relies on.
Friends-of-friends needs two relationship hops in a row, which this two-key KV table can't do without a graph database.
scenario: News Feed 只有 Follow 主表和它的反向 GSI，没有图数据库；要盘点这套结构支持哪些查询。
scenario_en: News Feed has only the Follow table plus its reverse GSI and no graph database, so we need to know which queries it can serve.

q: 补全 Follow 表的键设计：
q_en: Complete the key design for the Follow table.
text: Follow 主表：分区键 {{userFollowing}}、排序键 {{userFollowed}}；GSI 把两键反转，分区键为 {{userFollowed}}，用于查某用户的粉丝列表。
why: 键设计决定查询能力：主表服务『我关注了谁/是否关注』，反向 GSI 服务『谁关注我』。写扇出与读路径都建立在它上面。
why_en: The key design decides which queries are possible: the base table serves who I follow, and the reverse GSI serves who follows me.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

scenario: 你已经用 DynamoDB 分别建了 Post 表和 Follow 表，面试官追问生产环境的表设计惯例。
scenario_en: You have modeled separate Post and Follow tables in DynamoDB, and the interviewer asks about production table-design practice.
q: 关于 DynamoDB 的表设计，AWS 官方推荐的生产实践是什么？
q_en: What DynamoDB table-design practice does AWS recommend for production?
options: DynamoDB 不支持多张表
AWS 推荐单表，面试分表也可以
必须严格一个实体一张表
GSI 免费且数量无限，随便加
options_en: DynamoDB doesn't support multiple tables.
AWS recommends single-table design in production, but splitting tables for clarity in an interview is fine.
Every entity must strictly get its own table.
GSIs are free and unlimited, so add as many as you like.
why: 生产上 AWS 推荐把多个实体塞进一张表（single-table design）；面试里分表讲清楚完全没问题。
why_en: In production AWS recommends packing multiple entities into one table, but splitting tables for a clearer interview explanation is perfectly fine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一张 DynamoDB 表里存多种实体，用键设计区分类型，是 AWS 推荐的生产实践。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-table design stores multiple entity types in one DynamoDB table, distinguished by key design; it is AWS's recommended production pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

optionExplanations: DynamoDB 完全支持建多张表，这个说法本身就不成立。
对：生产上 AWS 推荐把多实体塞进一张表，但面试里分表讲更清楚也没问题。
『可以分表』不等于『必须分表』，把选项误读成了硬性规则。
GSI 既要花钱也有数量配额，不是想加多少加多少。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB fully supports creating multiple tables, so that claim is simply false.
Correct: in production AWS recommends packing multiple entities into one table, but splitting tables for interview clarity is perfectly fine.
'Tables can be split' gets misread as a hard rule that they must be, which isn't the same thing.
GSIs cost money and come with quotas, they're not something to add without limit.

scenario: 刷 feed 是重读负载，查询模式与发帖、关注完全不同，希望能独立扩缩容和演进。
scenario_en: Feed reads are heavy and have a very different query pattern from posting and following, so this logic should scale and evolve independently.
q: 架构上应该怎么组织这块逻辑？
q_en: How should the feed-generation logic be organized architecturally?
options: 并入 Post Service 一起处理
并入 Follow Service
拆出一个独立的 Feed Service
下放到客户端自行聚合
options_en: Fold it into the Post Service.
Fold it into the Follow Service.
Split it out into its own Feed Service.
Push it down to the client to aggregate itself.
why: feed 生成读多写少、查询模式独特，和发帖/关注放一起会互相拖累扩容；单独拆出 Feed Service 能独立优化读路径。
why_en: Feed generation is read-heavy with a distinct query pattern, so bundling it with posting or following would slow both down.
whenOtherWins: 系统和团队都很小时，先合在一个服务里更简单；过早拆分只会增加运维负担。
tradeoff: 独立扩容能力 vs 拆分带来的运维复杂度
optionExplanations: 写密集的 Post Service 兼管读密集的 feed，扩容时两种负载会互相拖累。
Follow Service 本职是维护关系图，让它兼管 feed 生成职责边界会很乱。
对：把读密集的聚合逻辑单独封装，团队才能各自定节奏发版，不必和发帖/关注抢同一次上线窗口。
把聚合逻辑下放给客户端，等于让每个设备重复做本该服务端集中做的工作。
optionExplanations_en: The write-heavy Post Service taking on the read-heavy feed means the two workloads would slow each other's scaling down.
The Follow Service's job is maintaining the relationship graph; bolting feed generation onto it blurs the boundary.
Correct: isolating the read-heavy aggregation logic lets each team ship on its own schedule instead of fighting over the same release window as posting or following.
Pushing aggregation down to the client just makes every device redo work the server should centralize once.

q: 把 naive（朴素）feed 生成的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the naive feed-generation steps in the right order.
steps: 把汇总的全部帖子按时间倒序排好，返回给用户
从 Follow 表查出该用户关注的所有账号
用 Post 表的 GSI 拉取这些账号的帖子
why: 朴素三步：拿关注列表 → 拉各账号帖子 → 排序返回。它功能正确，但每一步都会在规模变大时爆炸。
why_en: The naive flow is three steps: fetch the follow list, pull each account's posts, then sort and return, and it works correctly but every step explodes at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

scenario: 拿到关注列表后，要按时间序快速取出『这批 creator 的全部帖子』，而 Post 表目前只能按 postId 存取。
scenario_en: After getting the follow list, we need to fetch all posts by those creators in time order, but the Post table currently only supports postId access.
q: 怎么补上这个能力？
q_en: How do we add this access pattern?
options: 加 GSI：creatorId 分区、createdAt 排序
扫全表再按 creator 过滤
把每条帖子冗余复制进所有粉丝的行
在应用层内存里维护 creator 到 posts 的映射
options_en: Add a GSI to the Post table: partition key creatorId, sort key createdAt.
Scan the entire table and filter by creator in memory.
Duplicate every post into every follower's own row.
Maintain a creator-to-posts mapping in application memory.
why: GSI 用 creatorId 分区、createdAt 排序，就能按账号一次 range 查询拉出时间序的帖子，是 naive 读路径的基础索引。
why_en: A GSI partitioned by creatorId and sorted by createdAt lets a single range query return an account's posts in time order.
whenOtherWins: 彻底走预计算 feed 后主读路径不再依赖它，但未预计算大 V 的实时拉取仍需要这个 GSI。
tradeoff: 读侧一次 range 查询 vs 额外维护一个索引的写开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

optionExplanations: 对：新增这条二级索引后，原来的按 ID 点查表就多了一条按作者时间序检索的路径，且写路径不用改。
全表扫描再过滤是暴力解法，账号和帖子规模一大就直接跑不动。
把帖子提前复制进每个粉丝的行，这是写扇出方案该做的事，这里只是补一个读索引。
应用进程本身无状态，把这种持久映射放进内存，一重启就全丢了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: adding this secondary index gives the by-ID table a new time-ordered, by-author lookup path without touching the write side.
A full-table scan with filtering is a brute-force fallback that stops working once accounts and posts grow large.
Copying a post into every follower's row ahead of time is a write-fan-out move, not what this read-side index needs to do.
The app process itself is stateless, so keeping this persistent mapping in memory loses it on every restart.

q: 看到 naive feed 方案，应该立刻在心里拉响哪些警报？（多选）
q_en: What warning signs should you see in the naive feed design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 用户可能关注了大量账号
被关注的每个账号可能各有海量帖子
两者叠加，待排序的帖子总集可能非常大
DynamoDB 不支持按排序键做 range 查询
options_en: The user may follow a huge number of accounts.
Each followed account may have a huge number of posts.
Combined, the total set of posts to sort can become enormous.
DynamoDB can't range-query by sort key.
why: 三个警报同根同源：扇出。关注多则查询多，帖子多则每个查询返回多，乘起来排序集巨大。
why_en: All three alarms share one root cause, fan-out: more follows means more queries, more posts per account means bigger results, and multiplied together the sort set explodes.
optionExplanations: 用户关注账号越多，一次 feed 请求内部要打的下游查询就越多。
被关注账号帖子越多，每个查询回来的候选集合就越大。
两个因子相乘，待排序的候选集合规模会迅速失控。
GSI 排序键天生支持 range 查询，这条根本不是真实存在的限制。
optionExplanations_en: The more accounts a user follows, the more downstream queries one feed request fans out into.
The more posts a followed account has, the bigger the candidate set each of those queries returns.
Multiply the two factors together and the set waiting to be sorted spirals out of control fast.
A GSI's sort key naturally supports range queries, so this limitation doesn't actually exist.
scenario: naive 方案：读 feed 时现查关注列表再逐个拉帖。用户可关注数千账号，大 V 每天发几十条。
scenario_en: The naive design reads the follow list at request time and pulls posts one account at a time, while users follow thousands of accounts.

q: 为什么说 news feed 是『scaling reads』模式的教科书案例？
q_en: Why is a news feed a textbook scaling-reads problem?
options: 写远多于读
读写基本均衡，无从优化
内容无法缓存，只能加机器
读远多于写，且集中在近期内容
options_en: Writes far outnumber reads.
Reads and writes are roughly balanced, leaving nothing to optimize.
Content can't be cached, so the only lever is adding machines.
Reads vastly outnumber writes, and users mostly look at the first few items, so aggressively caching recent content pays off hugely.
why: feed 是典型读密集负载，且读集中在最新的少数几条上，所以预计算 feed、缓存近期帖子、聪明分页收益极高。
why_en: The feed is a classic read-heavy workload concentrated on the newest few items, which is exactly why precomputing feeds and caching recent posts pay off so well.
optionExplanations: 把读写比例说反了，这套系统恰恰是读远多于写。
读写并非均衡，这个假设直接排除了后面所有缓存和预计算的空间。
帖子内容其实极少改动，正好是最适合缓存的一类数据，说不能缓存是错的。
对：读远超写，且大部分读集中在最新的少数几条上，这是能吃缓存红利的关键。
optionExplanations_en: This reverses the ratio — the real workload here is reads far outnumbering writes.
Assuming reads and writes are balanced rules out all the caching and precomputation headroom that actually exists.
Post content barely changes, which makes it exactly the kind of data that caches well, so 'can't cache' is wrong.
Correct: reads vastly outnumber writes and concentrate on the newest handful of items, which is what makes caching pay off so well.
scenario: News Feed 每天的读请求是写请求的上百倍，且约 90% 的读落在最近 48 小时的帖子上。
scenario_en: News Feed serves roughly a hundred times more reads than writes, and about 90% of those reads hit posts from the last 48 hours.

scenario: News Feed 倒序翻页每页 20 条；服务端不为任何用户保存浏览位置，重启也要能续翻。
scenario_en: News Feed pages 20 posts at a time in reverse order, and the server keeps no per-user scroll position, so paging must survive a restart.
q: 用什么作为翻页游标最合适？
q_en: What is the best pagination cursor?
options: offset 页码
用户已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳
服务端会话里记录完整浏览位置
客户端回传全部已见 postId 列表
options_en: An offset page number.
The timestamp of the oldest post the user has already seen.
A full scroll position recorded in a server session.
The client sends back a list of every postId already seen.
why: 倒序浏览下游标 = 已见最旧帖的 createdAt；下一页 = createdAt < 游标 的 20 条，服务端零状态。
why_en: The cursor is just the createdAt of the oldest post you have seen, so the next page is simply the 20 posts older than it and the server stores nothing.
whenOtherWins: 排序不是纯时间（个性化打分）时，需要改用编码了排序键的不透明 cursor。
tradeoff: 无状态时间戳游标 vs 服务端存储的浏览位置

termDefinitions.meaning: 翻页用的标记，记录用户已看到的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor is a pagination marker recording how far a user has scrolled.

optionExplanations: 严格倒序展示下，新帖插入会让 offset 对应的记录整体错位。
对：倒序浏览时最旧已见帖子的时间戳一个数就够，下一页就是比它更旧的 N 条。
服务端为每个会话存完整浏览位置，等于给自己加了一份不必要的持久状态。
客户端携带全部已见 postId，这份列表只会越滚越大，白白浪费带宽。
optionExplanations_en: In a strict newest-first view, inserting new posts shifts what each offset actually points to.
Correct: in a newest-first feed, one timestamp for the oldest post seen is enough, since the next page is just the N posts older than it.
Storing a full scroll position per server session adds persistent state the design doesn't actually need.
Having the client carry every seen postId means that list only keeps growing, wasting bandwidth for nothing.

q: 为什么支持翻页几乎不需要新增任何基础设施？
q_en: Why does pagination need almost no new infrastructure here?
options: GSI 已按 createdAt 排序，加个过滤条件就行
把整套翻页逻辑全部丢给客户端自己去实现、维护并保存分页状态
DynamoDB 本身自带完整的页码翻页功能
因为这个 feed 场景其实完全不需要翻页
options_en: The GSI is already sorted by createdAt, so it just needs one added filter.
The whole pagination logic is dumped onto the client to implement, maintain, and store its own paging state.
DynamoDB itself comes with a complete built-in page-number feature.
Because this feed scenario doesn't actually need pagination at all.
why: GSI 的排序键就是 createdAt，range 查询天然支持『小于某时间戳』，翻页版流程只是多加了一个过滤条件。
why_en: Since the GSI is already sorted by createdAt, a range query naturally supports 'less than this timestamp', so pagination is just one extra filter on the existing flow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

optionExplanations: 对：翻页只是在已有索引上再加一个『小于游标』的过滤条件，没有引入新表或新索引。
把服务端该做的过滤逻辑推给客户端，反而要客户端自己重新实现分页判断。
DynamoDB 没有内置页码功能，这是对它能力的误解。
需求里明确写了要支持翻页，这个说法直接和题目要求矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: pagination is just one more 'less than the cursor' filter on an index that's already there, no new table or index needed.
Pushing this filtering logic to the client means it has to reimplement pagination judgment on its own.
DynamoDB has no built-in page-number feature — that's a misunderstanding of its capabilities.
The stated requirements explicitly ask for pagination, so this directly contradicts what the problem asks for.
scenario: News Feed 要加翻页，但这一轮不想引入新组件；帖子已经躺在按 createdAt 排序的 GSI 上。
scenario_en: We want pagination in News Feed without adding new infrastructure, and posts already sit in a GSI sorted by createdAt.

q: 补全带翻页的 feed 读取流程：
q_en: Complete the paginated feed read flow.
text: 翻页版流程：查出关注列表 → 拉取这些账号{{早于 cursor 时间戳}}的帖子 → 按时间{{倒序}}排序返回，并附上 {{nextCursor}} 供下一页使用。
why: 与 naive 流程唯一的区别是第二步多了时间过滤。cursor 向过去推进，每页都是更旧的内容。
why_en: The only difference from the naive flow is an added time filter in step two, and the cursor keeps moving further into the past with each page.

scenario: Feed Service 处理一次刷 feed 请求时，内部要挨个查询数百个被关注账号的帖子。
scenario_en: For one feed request, Feed Service internally queries posts from hundreds of followed accounts.
q: 什么是 fan-out on read？
q_en: What is fan-out on read?
options: 一次写请求触发多次下游写
一次读扇出成大量下游请求
读请求被复制到多个只读副本
缓存雪崩的另一种叫法
options_en: One write request triggers many downstream writes.
One read request fans out into many downstream requests inside the system, like querying hundreds of followed accounts to build one feed.
A read request gets replicated to multiple read replicas.
Another name for a cache stampede.
why: 读扇出 = 进来一个请求、内部炸开成许多请求。用户关注得越多，Follow 查询越慢、Post 查询越多，延迟越不可控。
why_en: Fan-out on read means one incoming request explodes into many internal requests, so the more accounts a user follows, the more unpredictable the latency gets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次读请求在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read means one read request gets amplified into many downstream requests inside the system.

optionExplanations: 一次写触发多次下游写，说的其实是写扇出，不是读扇出。
对：一次刷 feed 的读请求，在内部炸开成几百个查询各个被关注账号的下游请求。
只读副本路由是负载均衡手段，跟一个请求内部炸开成多个请求是两回事。
缓存雪崩指的是缓存大面积失效后请求全砸向数据库，和读扇出不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: One write triggering many downstream writes describes write fan-out, not read fan-out.
Correct: one feed-read request explodes internally into hundreds of queries against each followed account.
Routing reads across replicas is a load-balancing technique, a different thing from one request exploding into many.
A cache stampede is when mass cache expiry sends everything to the database at once — not the same thing as read fan-out.

scenario: 刷一次 feed 时，请求在内部会扇出成数十到上百次下游查询；面试官问你对扇出数量级的经验判断。
scenario_en: One feed refresh can fan out into tens or hundreds of downstream queries; the interviewer is asking for your order-of-magnitude judgment.
q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this fan-out scale support?
options: 扇出超过 10 个请求就不可接受
上千级扇出很常见，不必担心
几十到上百常见，上千级基本不可行
扇出数量与延迟无关
options_en: Any fan-out above 10 requests is unacceptable.
Fan-out in the thousands is common and nothing to worry about.
Tens to hundreds of fan-out requests are common, but thousands are basically unworkable for a low-latency service.
The amount of fan-out has no effect on latency.
why: 10s-100s 的扇出是正常工程现实；1000s 级别在延迟敏感的在线服务里几乎撑不住，这个量级感帮你判断何时必须换思路。
why_en: Tens to hundreds of fan-out requests are normal engineering reality, but thousands are nearly unworkable for a latency-sensitive service and signal it's time to precompute instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求或写入在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求或写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request or write gets amplified into many downstream requests or writes.

optionExplanations: 十几个下游请求在延迟敏感服务里完全扛得住，把上限卡在 10 太保守。
上千级扇出对低延迟在线服务几乎是灾难，说『不必担心』低估了代价。
对：几十到上百级扇出是工程日常，上千级基本撑不住，这个量级感能帮你判断何时该换思路。
扇出数量直接决定要并发等待多少个下游响应，跟延迟关系很大。
optionExplanations_en: Tens of downstream requests are perfectly sustainable for a latency-sensitive service, so capping at 10 is overly conservative.
Thousands of fan-out requests is close to disastrous for a low-latency online service, so 'nothing to worry about' underestimates the cost.
Correct: tens-to-hundreds of fan-out is normal engineering reality, while thousands is basically unworkable — this magnitude sense tells you when to switch approaches.
How much fan-out there is directly decides how many downstream responses you're waiting on concurrently, which drives latency a lot.

scenario: 关注数极大的用户读 feed 时扇出失控；而这个系统读远比写频繁、且容忍 1 分钟陈旧。
scenario_en: Users who follow huge numbers of accounts make read fan-out explode, while this system is read-heavy and tolerates one-minute staleness.
q: 优化的核心思路应该是？
q_en: What is the core optimization idea?
options: 把扇出搬到写时：发帖即预写各粉丝 feed
无限增加只读副本来硬扛查询压力
让客户端自己并行发起对全部关注对象的下游查询请求
把排序逻辑整个下放给 CDN 去处理
options_en: Move the work to write time: precompute each follower's feed the moment a post is created.
Keep adding an unlimited number of read replicas to brute-force the query load.
Let the client itself fire off downstream query requests to every followed account in parallel.
Push the entire sorting logic down to the CDN to handle.
why: 读多写少 + 容忍短暂陈旧 = 把昂贵的扇出搬到写路径：发帖时预写各粉丝的 feed，读的时候一次点查就够。
why_en: Being read-heavy and tolerant of brief staleness is exactly what justifies moving the expensive fan-out to write time, so a post prewrites into each follower's feed.
whenOtherWins: 对粉丝数百万的大 V，写扇出的代价反过来爆炸，这些账号应保留读时拉取。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写入（发帖）时就把结果预先分发到每个下游位置，而不是等读时再算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write means pushing results out to every downstream location at write time instead of computing them on read.

optionExplanations: 对：读多写少又能容忍陈旧，正好把昂贵的扇出提前挪到写路径，读时一次点查就够。
无限加只读副本只是把同样的扇出查询摊到更多机器上，扇出本身的形状没变。
让客户端并行发起所有查询，只是把服务端的扇出成本转嫁给用户设备和网络。
CDN 擅长分发静态内容，个性化排序这种动态逻辑不是它的强项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: being read-heavy and tolerant of staleness is exactly what justifies precomputing at write time, leaving reads as a single point query.
Adding unlimited read replicas just spreads the same fan-out queries across more machines without changing their shape.
Having the client fire all the queries in parallel just shifts the server's fan-out cost onto the user's device and network.
A CDN is built for distributing static content, not dynamic, personalized sorting logic.

scenario: 只有极少数用户关注了 10 万个账号；为这条长尾把整体架构复杂度拉满并不划算。
scenario_en: Only a tiny fraction of users follow 100,000 accounts, so optimizing the whole architecture for that tail is not worth it.
q: 如何处理这条长尾，避免为它抬高整体架构复杂度？
q_en: How should we handle this long tail without making the whole architecture more complex?
options: 坚持在技术上无条件支持无限关注
问面试官能否给关注数设上限
直接禁止这类用户使用产品
忽略这个边缘情况不谈
options_en: Insist on unconditionally supporting unlimited follows at any technical cost.
Check with the interviewer whether a follow cap is acceptable (like Facebook's 5000-friend limit), or give these users a slightly degraded experience.
Simply ban these users from the product.
Ignore this edge case and never mention it.
why: 生产系统对极端用户设上限或差异化体验很常见；和面试官确认『产品能不能改』既现实又展示产品意识。
why_en: Production systems commonly cap extreme users, and asking the interviewer whether the product can flex is realistic and shows product judgment.
whenOtherWins: 若无限关注被确认为硬性需求，就必须靠混合扇出等架构手段真正解决。
tradeoff: 产品层面设上限 vs 架构层面无限支持
optionExplanations: 为极少数长尾用户把整体架构复杂度拉满，性价比很差。
对：生产系统对极端用户设上限很常见，问面试官产品能不能这样改，既现实又体现产品判断。
直接把这批用户挡在产品外面是过度反应，问题本可以用更轻的方式解决。
已经识别到的问题选择不提，会让面试官觉得考虑不周全。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling up the whole architecture's complexity for a tiny long tail of users is a poor tradeoff.
Correct: production systems commonly cap extreme users, and asking whether the product can flex that way is realistic and shows product judgment.
Banning these users outright is an overreaction when a lighter fix would do.
Choosing not to mention a problem you've already spotted reads as incomplete thinking to an interviewer.

q: PrecomputedFeed 表的结构是什么样的？
q_en: What does the PrecomputedFeed table look like?
options: PK = postId，值是粉丝列表
PK = userId、SK = createdAt，每条帖子一行
PK=userId，值是倒序 postID 列表，截断约 200
一张宽表冗余存储帖子全文
options_en: Partition key postId, with a value holding the follower list.
Partition key userId, sort key createdAt, one row per post.
Partition key userId, with a value holding a reverse-chronological list of postIDs capped around 200, looked up only by userId.
A wide table redundantly storing full post text.
why: 每个用户一条紧凑条目：倒序 postID 列表、限长约 200，只按 userId 点查，因此零二级索引。
why_en: Each user gets one compact entry, a reverse-chronological postID list capped around 200, looked up only by userId with no secondary index needed.
optionExplanations: 把键设计反过来围着帖子转，这不是这张表该服务的查询方向。
每条帖子存一行，条目数会随粉丝数线性膨胀，违背『紧凑存储』的目标。
对：每用户一条紧凑条目，只按 userId 点查，倒序 postID 列表截断约 200 条。
把帖子全文也复制进这张表，存储量会远超只存 ID 列表的设计初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Inverting the key around the post instead of the user isn't the query direction this table needs to serve.
One row per post makes the entry count grow linearly with follower count, defeating the point of staying compact.
Correct: one compact entry per user, looked up only by userId, holding a reverse-chronological postID list capped around 200.
Duplicating full post text into this table would balloon storage far past what a plain ID list needs.
scenario: 设计 News Feed 的预计算表：读路径必须一次点查拿到 feed，且每人一份的存储成本要可控。
scenario_en: For the precomputed News Feed table, a read must be a single point lookup, and the per-user storage cost has to stay bounded.

q: feed 条目为什么只存 postID 列表、还截断在 200 条左右？
q_en: Why store only a list of postIDs in each feed entry and cap it around 200 items?
options: DynamoDB 单行只允许 2KB
200 是 SQS 的批量投递上限
客户端一次最多渲染 200 条
紧凑条目控制总存储，长尾靠回退方案
options_en: DynamoDB limits every row to 2KB.
200 is SQS's batch-delivery limit.
The client can render at most 200 items at once.
Keeping entries compact controls total storage at 2B users, and real users rarely scroll that deep, with a fallback covering those who do.
why: 紧凑条目 = 可控成本：10 字节的 postID × 200 条才 2KB。这个 200 可以按尾部用户受影响程度和成本权衡上下调。
why_en: A compact entry keeps cost controlled since 200 ten-byte postIDs is only 2KB, and this cap can be tuned up or down based on the tail impact and cost tradeoff.
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 单行限制是 400KB 不是 2KB，引用了错误的数字。
SQS 的批量投递限制和这张表的行大小设计完全是两件事。
客户端一次能渲染多少条是前端的事，不是决定后端存储上限的原因。
对：10 字节 postID×200 条只有 2KB，这是控制总存储的权衡，长尾靠回退方案兜底。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB's row limit is actually 400KB, not 2KB, so that cites the wrong number.
SQS's batch-delivery limit is an entirely separate concern from how big this table's row is.
How much a client can render at once is a frontend concern, not what caps the backend's storage design.
Correct: 200 ten-byte postIDs is only 2KB, a deliberate tradeoff to keep total storage controlled, with a fallback covering the tail.
scenario: 预计算 feed 要给十亿量级用户每人存一份，存储预算有限；只有极少数人会翻到很深。
scenario_en: We store one precomputed feed per user across a billion users on a tight storage budget, and very few people scroll deep.

q: 用户真的把 200 条预计算 feed 翻完了，系统怎么办？
q_en: What should the system do if a user really scrolls past the 200 precomputed feed items?
options: 返回空页并提示没有更多内容
从头循环再显示一遍
回退到 naive 路径现查更旧内容
系统必须为每人预存 10 万条以避免这种情况
options_en: Return an empty page saying there's no more content.
Loop back and show the same content again from the top.
Fall back to the naive path: query the Follow table and the Post table's GSI on demand for older content.
The system must pre-store 100,000 entries per user to avoid this.
why: 预计算只是快路径：200 条 ≈ 覆盖 99% 的会话；翻穿后回退到 naive 现查，代价是这部分请求变慢。
why_en: The precomputed feed is only the fast path covering about 99% of sessions; once you page past it we fall back to the naive on-demand query and accept a slower request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

optionExplanations: 翻穿了就直接返回空页，等于告诉用户没有更旧内容了，这不符合事实。
从头循环重复展示同样的内容，是掩盖数据不足的假象，体验是坏的。
对：预计算只是快路径，翻穿了就退回到按需查询 Follow 表和 Post 表的 naive 方案。
为避免这种罕见场景给每人都存 10 万条，存储成本会不成比例地暴涨。
optionExplanations_en: Returning an empty page once it runs out falsely tells the user there's no older content at all.
Looping back to show the same content again masks insufficient data behind a broken-feeling experience.
Correct: precomputation is only the fast path, so once it's exhausted the system falls back to the on-demand naive query.
Pre-storing 100,000 entries per user just to dodge this rare case would blow up storage cost disproportionately.
scenario: 用户一路下拉，翻穿了预计算 feed 里全部约 200 条，但产品不允许给他一个空白页。
scenario_en: A user keeps scrolling past all 200 entries in their precomputed feed, and the product cannot show them an empty page.

q: 在『读 feed 时要做多少工作』这个维度上，预计算 feed 和 naive 现查的对比是？
q_en: How do precomputed feeds and naive on-demand reads compare on read-path work?
options: 两者读时工作量一样，只差数据新旧
naive 更快，因为不用维护额外的表
预计算方案读时也要现场排序全部帖子
预计算一次点查；naive 现查+全量排序
options_en: Both do the same amount of read-time work, differing only in data freshness.
Naive is faster because it avoids maintaining an extra table.
The precomputed approach still sorts every post at read time.
Precomputed: one point query returns a ready list. Naive: fetch the follow list, query per account, then sort everything.
why: 预计算把『查 N 个账号 + 排序』的成本提前付掉，读路径退化成一次点查；代价转移到写路径。
why_en: Precomputation pays the cost of querying N accounts and sorting upfront, reducing the read path to a single point query while shifting the cost to writes.
tradeoff: 读时一次点查 vs 写时预付扇出成本
optionExplanations: 两者读时开销其实差得很远，说『只差新旧』忽略了真正的工作量差异。
naive 方案不用维护额外表没错，但代价是每次读都要现场查询加排序，反而更慢。
预计算方案的读路径已经不用现场排序了，这正是它存在的意义。
对：预计算一次点查直接拿到结果；naive 要先查 N 个账号再全量排序，工作量差一个数量级。
optionExplanations_en: The read-time cost of the two actually differs a lot; 'only freshness differs' misses the real workload gap.
Naive really does skip maintaining an extra table, but the price is querying and sorting fresh on every read, which is slower.
The precomputed approach's whole point is that its read path no longer needs to sort on the fly.
Correct: precomputed is one point query returning a ready list, while naive queries N accounts and sorts everything — an order-of-magnitude gap.
scenario: News Feed 读 QPS 是写的百倍、读延迟预算 200ms；要比较两种方案的读路径成本。
scenario_en: News Feed reads outnumber writes a hundred to one with a 200ms read budget, so we compare the read cost of the two designs.

q: 『如果用户往回翻 100 页怎么办？』的现实工程答案是？
q_en: What is the practical engineering answer to 'what if a user scrolls back 100 pages'?
options: 必须完整支持，不计成本
大多数系统不支持极深翻页
把全部历史缓存到客户端
为深翻页单独建一套集群
options_en: It must be fully supported, whatever the cost.
Most systems simply don't support very deep pagination, because real users never scroll that far.
Cache a user's entire history on the client.
Stand up a separate cluster just for deep pagination.
why: 深翻页是典型的『理论问题』：真实产品直接不支持或弱支持。敢说『这个场景我们选择不优化』本身就是成熟判断。
why_en: Very deep pagination is a classic theoretical concern that real products simply don't support well, and saying so out loud is itself a sign of engineering maturity.
optionExplanations: 为一个几乎不会发生的场景不计成本地完整支持，性价比很差。
对：真实用户几乎不会翻这么深，大多数产品直接不支持或弱支持极深翻页，这是现实的工程判断。
把服务端该解决的问题转嫁到客户端存储，只是换了个地方踩坑。
为几乎不会发生的深翻页单独建集群，投入和收益完全不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: Fully supporting a scenario that almost never happens, whatever the cost, is a poor tradeoff.
Correct: real users almost never scroll that deep, so most products simply don't support very deep pagination well — a realistic engineering call.
Shifting a server-side problem onto client-side storage just moves the pain somewhere else.
Standing up dedicated infrastructure for pagination that basically never happens is wildly disproportionate.
scenario: 产品数据显示 99.9% 的会话翻不过 5 页；面试官追问『用户往回翻 100 页怎么办』。
scenario_en: Product data shows 99.9% of sessions never go past five pages, and the interviewer asks what happens if someone pages back a hundred pages.

scenario: 预计算 feed 的存储估算：每个 postID 约 10 字节，每人保留约 200 条，系统约 20 亿用户。
scenario_en: Precomputed-feed storage estimate: each postID is about 10 bytes, each user keeps about 200 entries, and the system has about 2 billion users.
q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this storage estimate support?
options: 每用户 2KB，总计约 4TB——对现代系统完全可行
每用户 2MB，总计 4PB，不可行
每用户 20KB，总计 40TB，需要重新设计
每用户 200B，总计 400GB，可以忽略存储问题
options_en: About 2KB per user, roughly 4TB total, comfortably feasible for a modern system.
About 2MB per user, roughly 4PB total, infeasible.
About 20KB per user, roughly 40TB total, needing a redesign.
About 200B per user, roughly 400GB total, small enough to ignore storage entirely.
why: 10B × 200 = 2KB/人；2KB × 20 亿 = 4TB。动手把存储算出来再下结论『合理』，是面试里该展示的习惯。
why_en: 10 bytes times 200 entries is 2KB per user, and 2KB times 2 billion users is about 4TB, which is a comfortable number for a modern system.
optionExplanations: 对：10 字节×200 条=2KB/人，乘 20 亿约 4TB，这个量级对现代存储系统完全轻松。
把单条 postID 算成了 10KB 级别，多算了三个数量级，4PB 是被夸大的结果。
20KB/人相当于每条 postID 占 100 字节，跟实际的 10 字节相差一个数量级。
200B/人少算了一位，200 条乘 10 字节应该是 2000B 而不是 200B。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: 10 bytes times 200 entries is 2KB per user, times 2 billion users is roughly 4TB — comfortably feasible for a modern system.
This treats each postID as roughly 10KB, three orders of magnitude too high, which is how the inflated 4PB shows up.
20KB per user implies about 100 bytes per postID, ten times the actual 10-byte figure.
200B per user is short by a factor of ten: 200 entries times 10 bytes should be 2000 bytes, not 200.

scenario: 已知每用户 feed 存储约 2KB/月的成本，而 Facebook 每个美国用户年收入约 100 美元。
scenario_en: Per-user feed storage costs about 2KB per month, while Facebook earns roughly $100 per US user per year.
q: 判断这笔存储值不值，有条好用的经验法则是？
q_en: What rule of thumb helps decide whether this storage cost is worth it?
options: 和竞品的存储量对比
按每用户美元成本对比收入
只看总量是否超过 1PB
找存储团队审批预算
options_en: Compare total storage against competitors.
Convert cost to dollars per user or tenant and compare it against the revenue that user brings in; here it's a fraction of a cent a month, no problem.
Just check whether the total exceeds 1PB.
Ask the storage team to approve the budget.
why: 把成本折算到『每用户多少钱』再对比『每用户赚多少钱』，一句话就能证明设计经济上成立。
why_en: Converting cost to dollars per user and comparing it against revenue per user is a quick way to prove a design is economically sound.
optionExplanations: 跟竞品比存储量不知道对方的架构和用户规模，这个对比基准站不住。
对：把成本折算成每用户多少钱，再对比每用户带来的收入，一句话就能证明经济上成立。
只看总量是否超过某个阈值，忽略了这笔钱相对于收入到底算不算多。
找团队审批预算是流程动作，不是一个能自己算出『值不值』的判断方法。
optionExplanations_en: Comparing storage against competitors ignores their architecture and user base, so it's not a solid baseline.
Correct: converting cost to dollars per user and comparing it against per-user revenue proves in one line whether a design is economically sound.
Just checking whether the total crosses some threshold ignores whether that cost is actually large relative to revenue.
Asking the storage team to approve a budget is a process step, not a way to reason about whether it's worth it yourself.

q: 预计算 feed 大幅改善了读性能，但同时制造了什么新问题？
q_en: What new problem does precomputing the feed create?
options: 读延迟反而上升
feed 的时间顺序会错乱
存储成本失控到不可行
读扇出变成了写扇出
options_en: Read latency actually goes up.
The feed's time ordering gets scrambled.
Storage cost spirals out of control.
A single post from a high-follower account must efficiently update a million follower feeds; read fan-out has become write fan-out.
why: 扇出没有消失，只是从读路径搬到了写路径：粉丝越多，发帖时要更新的 feed 条目越多。
why_en: Fan-out hasn't disappeared, it has just moved from the read path to the write path, since more followers means more feed entries to update per post.
optionExplanations: 预计算恰恰是为了降低读延迟，说读延迟反而上升和它的目的相反。
预计算不改变排序逻辑本身，时间顺序还是按 createdAt 排。
存储成本前面已经算过是可控的 4TB 级别，不是失控。
对：扇出没消失，只是从读路径搬到写路径——粉丝越多，发帖时要更新的条目越多。
optionExplanations_en: Precomputing exists specifically to cut read latency, so claiming it goes up is the opposite of its purpose.
Precomputation doesn't change the sort logic itself; ordering still runs by createdAt.
Storage cost was already worked out earlier to be a controlled ~4TB, not something out of control.
Correct: fan-out hasn't disappeared, it moved from the read path to the write path — more followers means more feed entries to update per post.
scenario: 上线预计算 feed 后读延迟降到个位毫秒，但千万粉丝的账号发一条帖就要触达全部粉丝。
scenario_en: After shipping precomputed feeds reads drop to single-digit milliseconds, but one post from an account with ten million followers must reach all of them.

q: 补全选择 fan-out on write 的推理：
q_en: Complete the reasoning for choosing fan-out on write.
text: 敢把扇出搬到写时，是因为这个系统{{读}}远多于写，且非功能需求允许 {{1 分钟}}内的帖子陈旧——发帖后有一个短窗口，可以异步把 postId 写进各粉丝的 {{PrecomputedFeed}} 表。
why: 这是条件反射级的推理链：读密集 + 容忍陈旧 → 写时预计算。没有那 1 分钟窗口，异步扇出就不成立。
why_en: This is a reflexive chain: read-heavy plus staleness-tolerant leads directly to precomputing at write time.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统必须让新帖立刻对所有粉丝可见，就不能靠异步写扇出，只能读时拉取或同步写。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写入时把结果预先分发到每个下游位置，而不是等读时再算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write pre-distributes results to downstream locations at write time instead of computing them on read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按用户保存的预计算 feed 列表，读时可一次点查返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PrecomputedFeed is a per-user prebuilt feed list that can be returned with one point lookup.

q: 发帖时由 Post Service 同步『一口气』写完百万粉丝的 feed，为什么行不通？
q_en: Why can't Post Service synchronously blast feed writes to millions of followers?
options: DynamoDB 不支持批量写入
会破坏帖子的时间排序
单机连接/延迟撑不住，负载也不均
SQS 有消息大小限制
options_en: DynamoDB doesn't support batch writes.
It would break the post's time ordering.
A single host can't sustain the connection count or latency, and load becomes wildly uneven, with the host handling a celebrity's post pegged while others sit idle.
SQS has a message size limit.
why: 同步 blast 撑不住：1000 万条写 ÷ 单机数千并发 × 每条几 ms ≫ 200ms 预算；大 V 落到哪台机哪台被压垮。
why_en: Ten million writes divided by a few thousand concurrent slots per host blows straight past the 200ms budget, and whichever host draws the celebrity gets crushed.
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 是支持批量写入的，这个说法本身不成立。
同步写扇出和排序逻辑没关系，帖子该按什么排序不受它影响。
对：单机连接数和延迟窗口撑不住百万级同步写，各主机之间负载也会极端不均。
这一步还没引入 SQS，拿它的限制来解释是找错了对象。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB does support batch writes, so that claim doesn't hold.
Synchronous write fan-out has nothing to do with sort logic; post ordering is unaffected either way.
Correct: a single host's connection count and latency window can't sustain a million synchronous writes, and load across hosts ends up extremely uneven.
SQS isn't even in the picture at this step, so citing its limit is pointing at the wrong thing.
scenario: 千万粉丝的账号发帖，Post Service 想在请求线程里同步写完所有粉丝的 feed，预算 200ms。
scenario_en: An account with ten million followers posts, and Post Service wants to write every follower feed synchronously inside a 200ms request.

q: 同步 blast 写扇出的具体问题包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What concrete problems does synchronous write fan-out create? (Select all that apply.)
options: 单个 Post Service 主机能建立的连接数有限
在延迟预算内根本写不完百万条 feed
主机间负载严重不均：一台在写百万条、另一台几乎闲置
会把帖子内容本身写坏
options_en: A single Post Service host can only open so many connections.
There's no way to finish writing a million feeds within the latency budget.
Load is badly imbalanced across hosts, one writing a million entries while another sits nearly idle.
It would corrupt the post content itself.
why: 10^6 条写 ÷ 数千并发 × 每条几 ms ≫ 延迟预算，再加负载不均，任一条都足以否掉同步方案；数据本身不会写坏。
why_en: A million writes over a few thousand concurrent slots blows the latency budget and the load lands unevenly across hosts, so the data is fine but the capacity is not.
optionExplanations: 单台 Post Service 主机能撑的并发连接数是有硬上限的。
百万级同步写会直接打穿发帖返回的延迟预算，用户等不起。
一台主机在写百万条 feed，另一台几乎闲置，资源利用率极端不均。
扇出方式只影响容量和延迟，不会把帖子内容本身写坏。
optionExplanations_en: A single Post Service host can only sustain so many concurrent connections before hitting a hard ceiling.
A million synchronous writes would blow straight through the posting request's latency budget.
One host ends up writing a million feed entries while another sits nearly idle, wildly uneven resource use.
How fan-out is done affects capacity and latency, not whether the post content itself gets corrupted.
scenario: Post Service 在请求线程里同步为百万粉丝写 feed；单机并发上限数千，延迟预算 200ms。
scenario_en: Post Service writes feeds for a million followers inside the request thread, with a few thousand concurrent writes per host and a 200ms budget.

scenario: 系统允许发帖到 feed 可见之间有小于 1 分钟的延迟；要把百万级 feed 写摊平，且写入能力可水平扩容。
scenario_en: The system allows less than one minute from posting to feed visibility; it must spread million-scale feed writes and scale workers horizontally.
q: 写扇出应该怎么架构？
q_en: How should write fan-out be architected?
options: 发帖入队，异步 worker 车队消费更新
Post Service 同步向所有粉丝分片广播 RPC
用数据库触发器逐行触发更新
每小时跑一次批处理统一合并
options_en: On post creation, enqueue one message and let a fleet of async workers consume it and update follower feeds.
Have the Post Service synchronously broadcast RPCs to every follower shard.
Use database triggers to fire an update row by row.
Run one batch job every hour to merge everything at once.
why: 既然容忍延迟，就把写请求排进队列，让可横向扩容的 worker 车队慢慢消化，负载被抹平。
why_en: Since the system tolerates a short delay, queuing the writes and letting a horizontally scalable fleet of workers drain them smooths out the load.
whenOtherWins: 若产品要求发帖立刻全局可见（强一致），队列带来的延迟不可接受，只能回到读时拉取。
tradeoff: 队列+异步 worker 的可扩展性 vs 立即一致的同步写

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管消息队列服务，提供 at-least-once 投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's managed message queue that guarantees at-least-once delivery.

optionExplanations: 对：入队这一步本身很快，真正需要横向扩容的压力全部转移到了消费队列的 worker 车队身上。
换成 RPC 广播本质还是同步阻塞，单机连接和延迟的老问题原样保留。
把扇出逻辑塞进数据库触发器，触发器执行在事务里，百万级更新会拖垮数据库本身。
固定每小时合并一次，新帖要等最多一小时才可见，超出了『小于 1 分钟』的要求。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: enqueueing itself stays fast, and all the pressure to scale horizontally shifts onto the fleet of workers draining the queue.
Switching to RPC broadcast is still synchronous under the hood, so the same single-host connection and latency problems remain.
Burying fan-out logic in a database trigger runs it inside a transaction, and a million updates there would drag the database down.
A fixed hourly batch means a new post can take up to an hour to appear, blowing past the under-one-minute requirement.

q: 对这条写扇出队列的硬性要求是什么？
q_en: What hard guarantee does the write fan-out queue need?
options: 必须提供严格的 exactly-once（精确一次）投递语义
必须严格保证 FIFO 顺序投递
支持 at-least-once 投递、高度可扩展即可
必须是自建的 Kafka 集群
options_en: It must offer strict exactly-once, deliver-exactly-one-copy semantics.
It must strictly guarantee FIFO-ordered delivery.
At-least-once delivery plus high scalability is enough.
It must specifically be a self-hosted Kafka cluster.
why: 任何满足 at-least-once + 可扩展的队列都行，at-least-once 意味着可能重复投递，worker 的更新要能容忍重复。
why_en: Any queue that offers at-least-once delivery and scales horizontally works, and since at-least-once can redeliver, the worker's update logic just needs to tolerate duplicates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息投递语义：消息不会丢，但可能被重复投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message is never lost but may be delivered more than once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is repeated.

optionExplanations: exactly-once 语义实现更复杂、成本更高，这里的更新逻辑没这个必要。
严格 FIFO 要求消息按顺序处理，但每个粉丝的 feed 更新之间互不依赖顺序。
对：托管队列如 SQS 默认就是这个语义，worker 只要把更新写成幂等操作就行，不用额外造轮子。
指定必须自建 Kafka 是把具体产品选型当成了硬性要求，其实任何合格队列都行。
optionExplanations_en: Exactly-once semantics are harder and pricier to implement, and this update logic doesn't actually need that guarantee.
Strict FIFO requires messages processed in order, but each follower's feed update doesn't depend on any particular order.
Correct: a managed queue like SQS offers exactly this by default, so the worker just needs its update to be idempotent, no extra plumbing required.
Requiring a self-hosted Kafka mistakes one specific product choice for a hard requirement — any adequate queue works.
scenario: 写扇出改走消息队列：日均千万条消息、峰值十倍，而 worker 的 feed 更新可重复执行。
scenario_en: Fan-out now goes through a queue with tens of millions of messages a day and ten-times peaks, and the feed update is safe to repeat.

scenario: 发帖后要异步给百万粉丝更新 feed；队列消息体有大小上限，入队必须在发帖请求内完成。
scenario_en: After a post we asynchronously update a million follower feeds; the queue caps message size and enqueueing must finish inside the post request.
q: 消息内容与 worker 逻辑，哪种设计正确？
q_en: Which message payload and worker behavior is correct?
options: 消息内嵌帖子全文，worker 直接推送给所有在线粉丝
消息只带 postId 和作者 id，worker 查粉丝写 feed
发帖方先在请求内查好全部粉丝列表塞进消息体，worker 只负责写入
worker 定期轮询扫描整张 Post 表，发现新帖再更新
options_en: Embed the full post body in the message and have the worker push it to every online follower.
Put only postId and author id in the message; the worker looks up followers and writes feeds.
Have the publisher resolve the whole follower list inside the request, stuff it into the message body, and leave the worker only to write.
Have workers poll the entire Post table on a timer to discover new posts and update feeds.
why: 消息保持最小（postId + creatorId），粉丝查询和 feed 更新都留给 worker 做，入队快、扩容压力在 worker 侧。
why_en: Keeping the message minimal, just postId and creatorId, lets the worker do the lookup and update, so enqueueing stays fast.
whenOtherWins: 粉丝量巨大时，一条消息可拆成多条、各带一段粉丝区间，避免单条消息的工作量畸大。
tradeoff: 消息小+worker 承担查询 vs 消息大+发帖方预先查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

optionExplanations: 把帖子全文塞进消息，消息体会随帖子长度膨胀，队列吞吐反而受拖累。
对：消息只带 postId 和 creatorId，粉丝查询和 feed 更新都交给 worker，入队快、扩容压力全在 worker 侧。
让发帖方先查好全部粉丝再入队，等于把 worker 该做的查询提前搬回发帖这条延迟敏感的路径。
定期扫表发现新帖是轮询模式，天然比事件驱动多一层延迟和浪费的扫描。
optionExplanations_en: Embedding the full post text bloats the message with post length, which drags down queue throughput.
Correct: the message carries only postId and creatorId, leaving follower lookup and the feed update to the worker, so enqueueing stays fast.
Having the poster look up every follower before enqueueing moves the worker's own query work back into the latency-sensitive posting path.
Periodically scanning the table for new posts is a polling pattern, adding delay and wasted scans that event-driven consumption avoids.

q: 异步 worker 方案落地后，仍然要面对的挑战是？
q_en: What challenge remains after moving fan-out to async workers?
options: 投递队列会随机把消息丢掉
SQS 这类托管队列的费用高到不可行
系统再也无法保证同一 feed 里帖子的最终时间排序
worker 总吞吐大，单条消息工作量方差极大
options_en: The delivery queue randomly loses messages.
A managed queue like SQS costs prohibitively high at this scale.
The system can no longer guarantee the final time ordering of posts within a feed.
The worker fleet needs enormous total throughput, and per-message work varies wildly.
why: 小账号几百次写不算什么，大账号一条消息就是百万级工作，方差极大意味着大任务可能需要拆分。
why_en: A small account's writes are trivial, but one message for a mega account can mean millions of updates, so huge tasks may need splitting.
optionExplanations: at-least-once 队列的保证恰恰是不会随机丢消息，这个说法搞反了。
托管队列的成本在这个量级下并不算高，这是夸大了它的开销。
排序逻辑跟异步化无关，feed 依然按帖子的 createdAt 排序。
对：小账号一条消息才几百次写，大账号一条消息就是百万级写，方差极大意味着大任务可能得拆分。
optionExplanations_en: An at-least-once queue's whole guarantee is that it won't randomly drop messages — this gets it backwards.
A managed queue's cost at this scale isn't actually prohibitive; this overstates the expense.
Ordering logic has nothing to do with going async; the feed still sorts by each post's createdAt.
Correct: a small account's message is a few hundred writes, a mega account's is millions — that huge variance means big tasks may need splitting.
scenario: 写扇出 worker 已上线：普通用户几百粉丝、头部账号千万粉丝，同一队列混着两类消息。
scenario_en: The fan-out workers are live: normal users have hundreds of followers and top accounts have millions, all mixed in one queue.

scenario: 某账号有 9000 万+粉丝，发一条帖等于 9000 万次 feed 写入，队列也救不动。
scenario_en: One account has 90 million or more followers, so one post would mean 90 million feed writes; even the queue cannot make that cheap.
q: 『great』级别的混合方案是？
q_en: What is the 'great' hybrid fan-out design?
options: 为大 V 建一条更大的专用队列
限制大 V 的发帖频率
高粉账号打 flag 跳过预计算，读时合并
把大 V 的帖子通过长连接直接推送到所有在线客户端
options_en: Build an even bigger dedicated queue just for celebrities.
Rate-limit how often celebrities can post.
Flag high-follower accounts as 'skip precomputation': async workers ignore them, and the feed read merges in their recent posts separately.
Push a celebrity's post directly to every online client over a persistent connection.
why: 对头部账号放弃写扇出、改回读时拉取：Follow 表打 flag，worker 忽略，读侧合并，9000 万次写就此绕开。
why_en: For top accounts, this gives up write fan-out and falls back to read-time pulling, flagging them in the Follow table so workers skip them.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统里根本没有头部账号，全员统一 fan-out on write 更简单，犯不着做混合。
tradeoff: 头部账号读时合并 vs 全员统一写扇出
optionExplanations: 队列做得再大，9000 万次写这个数量级问题本质没变。
限制大 V 的发帖频率是在改变产品行为去迁就架构，本末倒置。
对：给高粉账号打 flag，worker 跳过预计算，读时把他们的近期帖子现拉进来合并，绕开 9000 万次写。
把帖子直接推送到全部客户端既不现实也没有寻址机制支撑。
optionExplanations_en: No matter how big the queue gets, the order-of-magnitude problem of 90 million writes doesn't change.
Rate-limiting how often celebrities post changes product behavior to accommodate the architecture, which is backwards.
Correct: flagging high-follower accounts to skip precomputation and merging their recent posts in at read time sidesteps the 90-million-write problem entirely.
Pushing a post directly to every client is neither realistic nor something the system has addressing for.

q: 混合方案下，用户请求 feed 时 Feed Service 具体做什么？
q_en: In the hybrid design, what does Feed Service do when a user requests their feed?
options: 只读预计算表，忽略大 V
读 feed 时把整个内容全部现场拉取并重新计算排序
随机在两种方式里选一种
预计算部分+大 V 近期帖子，读时合并
options_en: Only read the precomputed table and ignore celebrities.
On every request, fetch the entire feed on the fly and recompute its ordering from scratch.
Randomly pick one of the two approaches each time.
Fetch the (partial) precomputed feed, pull recent posts from un-precomputed celebrity accounts, and merge them at read time.
why: 读路径变成两段拼接：Feed 表里的预计算部分 + 被 flag 账号的实时近期帖子，绝大多数内容仍走快路径。
why_en: The read path becomes a two-part merge: the precomputed part from the Feed table plus real-time recent posts from flagged accounts, with most content still on the fast path.
optionExplanations: 只读预计算表会漏掉被 flag 账号的内容，用户体验不完整。
全部现场重算等于放弃了预计算带来的全部读性能收益。
随机在两种方式里选一种没有依据，行为完全不可预测。
对：Feed Service 先查预计算表拿大部分内容，再单独查被 flag 账号的近况补齐，两边拼成一份结果。
optionExplanations_en: Reading only the precomputed table would drop content from flagged accounts, leaving an incomplete feed.
Recomputing everything from scratch throws away all the read-performance gains precomputation bought.
Randomly picking between the two approaches has no rationale and makes behavior unpredictable.
