Correct: Feed Service first reads the precomputed table for most content, then separately fetches flagged accounts' recent posts and stitches the two together.
scenario: 混合方案里，粉丝数超阈值的大 V 不做写扇出；用户请求 feed 的延迟预算仍是 200ms。
scenario_en: In the hybrid design we skip write fan-out for celebrities above a follower threshold, while the feed read budget stays at 200ms.

scenario: 面试官追问：所以到底应该选 fan-out on write 还是 fan-out on read？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether the system should use fan-out on write or fan-out on read.
q: 体现设计成熟度的回答是？
q_en: Which answer shows design maturity?
options: 不必一刀切：按账号粒度分别选择，大多数用户其实两者兼用
永远 fan-out on write，读性能至上
永远 fan-out on read，写成本至上
看数据库品牌决定
options_en: It doesn't need to be one-size-fits-all: choose per account, and most users actually get a bit of both.
Always fan-out on write, read performance above all.
Always fan-out on read, write cost above all.
It depends on the database vendor.
why: 混合方案的精髓：同一系统内按对象特征分别施策，不需要 one-size-fits-all 的答案。
why_en: The essence of the hybrid design is applying different strategies within the same system based on each account's characteristics, instead of forcing one-size-fits-all.
whenOtherWins: 小规模或账号分布均匀的系统里，统一策略更简单，混合方案的复杂度只有存在头部账号时才值得。
tradeoff: 按账号分层的混合策略 vs 全局统一策略
optionExplanations: 对：不必二选一，按账号特征分别施策——大多数普通用户走写扇出，极少数大 V 走读时合并。
永远走写扇出，会在大 V 账号上撞上百万级写的老问题，没解决根本矛盾。
永远走读时拉取，会让普通用户每次刷 feed 都承受不必要的扇出延迟。
这个选择由读写模式和账号分布决定，跟具体用哪家数据库没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: it doesn't need to be one-size-fits-all — most ordinary users get write fan-out, and a handful of mega accounts get read-time merging.
Always fan-out on write runs straight back into the millions-of-writes problem for celebrity accounts, the core issue unsolved.
Always fan-out on read forces every ordinary user to pay unnecessary fan-out latency on every single scroll.
This choice is driven by read/write patterns and account distribution, not by which database vendor is in use.

q: 混合扇出方案的代价是什么，怎么调节？
q_en: What is the cost of hybrid fan-out, and how can it be tuned?
options: 写路径整体变慢，无法调节
读时合并变贵，靠阈值调节平衡
存储直接翻倍
必须升级为强一致数据库
options_en: The whole write path gets slower, with no way to tune it.
Reads now require merging, increasing the Feed Service's compute cost; the follower-count threshold for skipping precomputation can be tuned to balance it.
Storage simply doubles.
The database must be upgraded to strong consistency.
why: 把合并从写时挪到读时，读侧 CPU 变贵；阈值调高则读更省、写更贵，反之亦然，可按负载调优。
why_en: Moving the merge to read time adds compute cost there, and the follower-count threshold is a knob trading cheaper reads for pricier writes.
optionExplanations: 写路径本身没有变慢，被 flag 的大 V 反而跳过了写扇出，这个说法归错了方向。
对：合并从写时挪到读时，读侧计算变贵；调高粉丝数阈值能让读更省、写更贵地权衡。
存储没有翻倍，这套方案改变的是计算发生的时机，不是存储量本身。
混合扇出方案不改变系统的一致性模型，跟升级数据库没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: The write path itself didn't get slower — flagged celebrities actually skip write fan-out — so this points at the wrong thing.
Correct: moving the merge to read time adds compute cost there, and the follower-count threshold is a tunable knob trading cheaper reads for pricier writes.
Storage doesn't double; this design changes when computation happens, not how much gets stored.
A hybrid fan-out design doesn't touch the consistency model, so it has nothing to do with upgrading the database.
scenario: 混合扇出上线后要调那个粉丝数阈值：读 QPS 是写的百倍，但大 V 写扇出也压着写路径。
scenario_en: With hybrid fan-out live we tune the follower threshold: reads outnumber writes a hundred to one, but celebrity fan-out still loads the write path.

q: 补全混合扇出的机制：
q_en: Complete the hybrid fan-out mechanism.
text: 混合扇出：在 {{Follow}} 表上给高粉账号的关注关系打上不预计算的 flag；{{异步 worker}} 消费队列时跳过这些账号；读 feed 时把预计算列表与这些大 V 的{{近期帖子}}合并。
why: 三个环节缺一不可：flag 标在关注关系上、worker 侧忽略、读侧补拉合并，让扇出策略精确到账号粒度。
why_en: All three parts are required together, the flag on the follow relationship, the worker skipping it, and the read-side merge, giving fan-out strategy per-account precision.

q: 把『大 V 发帖如何扇出』的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the celebrity-post fan-out decision chain in the right order.
steps: 升级：给高粉账号打 flag 跳过预计算，读时再合并其近期帖子
需求：大 V 发帖要写入百万级粉丝的 feed，但系统容忍 <1 分钟延迟
缓解：读侧合并增加的计算量，用粉丝数阈值调节预计算的范围
选型：发帖消息进 SQS，由异步 worker 车队执行写扇出
代价：消息工作量方差巨大，9000 万粉丝的账号写扇出仍不可行
why: 完整链条：容忍延迟的需求 → 队列+异步 worker → 头部账号仍爆炸 → 打 flag 混合扇出 → 用阈值调节读写平衡。
why_en: The chain runs from a delay-tolerant requirement, to a queue of async workers, to top accounts still exploding, to hybrid flagging with a tunable threshold.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有高粉账号，统一 fan-out on write 更简单，不需要引入 flag 和读时合并。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管消息队列服务，提供 at-least-once 投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's managed message queue that guarantees at-least-once delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时把 postId 写进粉丝 feed，读路径因此更便宜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write writes the postId into follower feeds at post time, making reads cheaper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刷 feed 时现场拉取并合并关注对象的帖子，写路径因此更便宜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read pulls and merges followed accounts' posts when the feed is read, making writes cheaper.

scenario: 系统里同时评估了发帖时预计算 feed、和刷 feed 时现查现拼这两种扇出策略。
scenario_en: The system evaluates both precomputing feeds at write time and assembling feeds on demand at read time.
q: fan-out on write 与 fan-out on read 在『代价发生在什么时候』上的区别是？
q_en: How do fan-out on write and fan-out on read differ in when the cost is paid?
options: on write：读时干活；on read：写时干活
两者的代价完全相同
on write 写贵读省；on read 写省读贵
两者都把代价推给后台批处理
options_en: On write: the work happens at read time; on read: the work happens at write time.
The two have exactly the same cost profile.
On write: a post fills every follower's feed upfront, so reads are cheap and writes are expensive; on read: the feed is assembled on the fly, so writes are cheap and reads are expensive.
Both push their cost onto a background batch job.
why: 预计算把成本搬到写路径（粉丝多则写爆炸），现查把成本留在读路径（关注多则读爆炸）；谁便宜取决于读写比例。
why_en: Precomputing moves cost onto the write path since more followers means bigger writes, while on-demand reads keep cost on the read path instead.
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read
optionExplanations: 把两种模式各自付出代价的时机说反了。
两者代价完全不对称，说『完全相同』忽视了它们本质上是相反的取舍。
对：fan-out on write 把成本提前付在写路径，读时一次点查；on read 把成本留到读时现查现拼。
两种模式都是实时路径上的直接取舍，都不依赖后台批处理来消化。
optionExplanations_en: This swaps which mode incurs its cost at which time.
The two costs are far from identical; calling them 'exactly the same' ignores that they're opposite tradeoffs.
Correct: fan-out on write pays the cost upfront on the write path so reads are a single point query, while fan-out on read leaves the cost on the read path instead.
Neither mode relies on a background batch job to absorb the cost; both are direct tradeoffs on the real-time path.

scenario: 非功能需求写明：系统容忍最多 1 分钟的帖子陈旧。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement says the system tolerates at most one minute of post staleness.
q: 写扇出必须在多长时间内完成？这个预算从哪来？
q_en: How quickly must write fan-out finish, and where does that budget come from?
options: 1 秒内，来自用户体验直觉
约 1 分钟，来自陈旧上限要求
1 小时内，批处理惯例
没有明确时限
options_en: Within 1 second, based on a UX intuition.
About 1 minute, taken directly from the non-functional requirement's staleness ceiling.
Within 1 hour, following batch-processing convention.
There is no defined deadline.
why: 非功能需求写明容忍 <1 分钟陈旧，这就是异步扇出的全部时间预算，需求里的数字最终都会变成设计约束。
why_en: The non-functional requirement caps staleness at under a minute, and that number becomes the entire time budget for async fan-out.
optionExplanations: 1 秒级预算没有依据支撑，题目给的容忍上限比这宽松得多。
对：非功能需求写明容忍不到 1 分钟的陈旧，这个数字直接就是异步扇出的时间预算。
1 小时是批处理的经验节奏，但这里明确要求的是分钟级，不是小时级。
题目已经给出明确的陈旧上限，说『没有时限』是没看这条约束。
optionExplanations_en: A one-second budget has no basis here — the stated tolerance is far looser than that.
Correct: the non-functional requirement caps staleness at under a minute, and that number directly becomes the async fan-out's time budget.
An hour fits typical batch-processing cadence, but the requirement here is explicitly minute-scale, not hour-scale.
The problem already states a clear staleness ceiling, so claiming there's no deadline ignores that constraint.

q: 帖子的读取生命周期通常是什么样的？
q_en: What does a post's read lifecycle usually look like?
options: 多数帖子几天转冷；爆款头几小时爆读
所有帖子的读量均匀分布
越老的帖子读得越多
帖子的读取完全随机分布，没有任何规律可循
options_en: Most posts go nearly unread after a few days, while a high-follower account's post gets an explosive burst of reads in its first few hours.
Read volume is spread evenly across all posts.
Older posts get read more than newer ones.
A post's reads are distributed completely at random, with no discernible pattern at all.
why: 读取高度偏斜且集中在近期：绝大多数帖子热几天，爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，这决定了缓存收益极高。
why_en: Reads skew heavily toward recent content, since most posts stay hot for only days while a viral post bursts in its first hours.
optionExplanations: 对：多数帖子几天内就没人看了，爆款账号的帖子在发布头几小时读量暴涨，这正是缓存能吃到红利的模式。
假设读量在所有帖子间均匀分布，等于假设没有热点，这和真实使用行为不符。
把读取规律说反了，实际是越新的帖子读得越多，不是越老。
读取完全随机意味着没有任何模式可利用，但真实数据明显偏向近期和热门内容。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: most posts go nearly unread after a few days, while a high-follower account's post gets a burst of reads in its first hours — exactly the pattern caching pays off on.
Assuming reads spread evenly across all posts assumes away hotspots entirely, which doesn't match real usage.
This reverses the actual pattern — newer posts get read far more than older ones, not the other way around.
Fully random reads would mean no exploitable pattern exists, but real traffic clearly skews toward recent and popular content.
scenario: 要给 Post 缓存定容量和 TTL，先看真实读取分布：feed 只展示近期帖，偶尔出现爆款。
scenario_en: Before sizing the post cache and its TTL we look at the real read distribution: feeds show recent posts, with occasional viral ones.

scenario: 某条爆款帖子 Post1 独占了分区的大量读请求，其余帖子所在分区几乎没有流量。
scenario_en: A viral post, Post1, takes a large share of reads on one partition while partitions for other posts are nearly idle.
q: DynamoDB 能扩到极高吞吐的关键前提是什么？违反了会怎样？
q_en: What condition lets DynamoDB scale to very high throughput, and what happens when it is violated?
options: 用最新代的存储实例
开启自动备份
把每个分区的预置吞吐量一次性买得足够高
负载必须均匀，否则热分区成瓶颈
options_en: Using the newest generation of storage hardware.
Turning on automatic backups.
Provisioning each partition's throughput high enough up front.
Load must be spread evenly across the keyspace; if one post hogs the requests while others get none, a hot partition becomes the bottleneck.
why: 『可无限扩展』的 KV store 都有同一行小字：负载要均匀。爆款帖子恰恰制造极端不均，这是热分区问题的根源。
why_en: Every 'infinitely scalable' key-value store hides the same fine print, load must stay even, and a viral post creates exactly the kind of imbalance that breaks it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载集中在少数几个分区、其余分区却很空闲的不均衡状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot partition is a shard that receives far more load than the others, breaking even distribution.

optionExplanations: 换用什么代的硬件跟负载是否均匀没有关系，这是无关选项。
自动备份是可靠性手段，跟吞吐能不能扩展没有关系。
预置吞吐买得再高，负载一旦极端不均，单个热分区照样会被打爆。
对：这是分区式存储的通用代价——某个键的流量一旦远超其他键，那个分区就先被打满。
optionExplanations_en: Which hardware generation is in use has nothing to do with whether load is spread evenly.
Automatic backups are a durability feature, unrelated to whether throughput can scale.
No matter how high provisioned throughput goes, a badly uneven load still overwhelms one hot partition.
Correct: this is the universal cost of partitioned storage — once one key's traffic dwarfs the rest, that single partition maxes out first.

q: 帖子数据有一个对缓存非常友好的性质，是什么？
q_en: What property of post data makes it very cache-friendly?
options: 帖子都很小，内存随便放
帖子没有多媒体内容
创建远多于编辑，长 TTL 安全
用户根本不在乎自己看到的帖子内容是否最新
options_en: Posts are all tiny, so memory is never a concern.
Posts never contain multimedia content.
Posts are almost only ever created, rarely edited, so the cache can safely use a long TTL.
Users simply don't care whether the post content they see is up to date.
why: 『创建远多于编辑』意味着缓存内容几乎不会过时：长 TTL 安全，只需在罕见编辑发生时精确失效。
why_en: Since posts are almost only created and rarely edited, cached content almost never goes stale, making a long TTL safe with precise invalidation only on the rare edit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 帖子大小和缓存友好性是两回事，小对象不代表就该长 TTL。
帖子完全可能带图片视频等多媒体内容，这个假设不成立。
对：帖子创建远多于编辑，意味着缓存内容几乎不会过时，长 TTL 很安全。
用户当然在意内容是否最新，缓存友好靠的是数据本身极少变化，不是用户的容忍度。
optionExplanations_en: Post size and cache-friendliness are separate things; a small object doesn't by itself justify a long TTL.
Posts absolutely can include images or video, so this assumption doesn't hold.
Correct: creation vastly outnumbering edits means cached content almost never goes stale, making a long TTL safe.
Users do care whether content is fresh — cache-friendliness comes from the data barely changing, not from user tolerance.
scenario: Post 缓存要定 TTL：产品里帖子发出后极少被编辑，而读量高度集中在最近几天。
scenario_en: We're picking a TTL for the post cache: posts are almost never edited after publishing, and reads concentrate on the last few days.

scenario: 爆款帖子的读流量正在打爆 Post 表的单个分区；帖子创建后极少被修改。
scenario_en: A viral post is overwhelming one Post-table partition, and posts are rarely modified after creation.
q: 『good』级别的解法是？
q_en: What is the 'good' solution for hot post reads?
options: 加分布式缓存：Redis 长 TTL + LRU
把 DynamoDB 的预置读吞吐量直接调高十倍来硬扛
把帖子搬到 S3
限制单条帖子的阅读次数
options_en: Insert a distributed cache between readers and the Post table: shard by postId on a Redis cluster, with a long TTL and LRU eviction.
Provision DynamoDB's read throughput ten times higher to brute-force it.
Move posts into S3.
Cap how many times a single post can be read.
why: 只要缓存装得下大多数近期帖子，绝大部分读就不再落库；长 TTL 可行是因为帖子极少编辑，LRU 自动腾出冷帖空间。
why_en: As long as the cache holds most recent posts, most reads never hit the database, and a long TTL is safe because posts are rarely edited while LRU frees space for cold posts.
whenOtherWins: 若读负载本来均匀、量级不大，DynamoDB 直查就够，缓存只是多余的复杂度。
tradeoff: 缓存吸收热点读 vs 直查数据库的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略，优先清掉最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU evicts the entry that has gone the longest without being accessed.

optionExplanations: 对：在数据库前插一层缓存，把重复的热点读挡在数据库之外，只有真正的 miss 才落库。
花十倍预算硬扛，不解决负载分布不均本身，成本还会持续线性上涨。
S3 是为大对象和静态分发设计的，不适合这种低延迟点查场景。
限制单条帖子的阅读次数会直接违背『帖子能被大量浏览』的产品目标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: inserting a cache layer in front of the database intercepts repeated hot reads before they reach the database, only real misses fall through.
Paying for ten times the throughput brute-forces the symptom without fixing the underlying load imbalance, and the bill keeps climbing linearly.
S3 is built for large objects and static distribution, not this kind of low-latency point lookup.
Capping how many times a post can be read directly contradicts the product goal of letting posts be widely viewed.

q: Post 缓存在什么时机做失效（invalidate）？
q_en: When should the Post cache be invalidated?
options: 每次有新帖创建时就把整个缓存全量失效
编辑时按 postId 精确失效
每小时定时清空
永不失效，全靠 TTL
options_en: Flush the entire cache every single time any new post is created.
Precisely invalidate by postId only when a post is edited; a new post needs no invalidation.
Clear the whole cache on a fixed hourly schedule.
Never invalidate at all, relying purely on TTL.
why: 新帖不存在缓存里，谈不上失效；只有编辑会让缓存变陈旧，只需在编辑时删掉对应 postId 的条目。
why_en: A new post was never cached, so there's nothing to invalidate, and only an edit makes the cache stale, so deleting that one postId is enough.
optionExplanations: 新帖当时根本还没进缓存，谈不上要为它做失效。
对：只有编辑会让缓存陈旧，只需在编辑那一刻删掉对应 postId 的条目就够了。
按小时定时清空和真正的编辑事件完全脱钩，清早了浪费、清晚了脏读。
完全放弃主动失效，编辑后的旧内容会一直留到 TTL 自然到期才消失。
optionExplanations_en: A brand-new post was never in the cache yet, so there's nothing to invalidate for it.
Correct: only an edit makes the cache stale, so deleting just that one postId at the moment of the edit is all that's needed.
A fixed hourly flush is completely decoupled from actual edit events — too early wastes work, too late serves stale reads.
Giving up active invalidation entirely leaves edited content stale until the TTL naturally times out.
scenario: Post 缓存命中率约 95%，用户偶尔会编辑帖子；失效策略不能让每次发帖都抖动缓存。
scenario_en: The post cache runs at about 95% hit rate and users occasionally edit posts, so invalidation must not churn the cache on every new post.

scenario: 分布式帖子缓存由 N 台主机组成，每台主机有 M 内存。
scenario_en: The distributed post cache has N hosts, and each host has M memory.
q: 这个集群总容量怎么估算，说明了什么？
q_en: How do we estimate total cache-cluster capacity, and what does it imply?
options: 等于单台主机的内存 M
等于数据库的总大小
无法用公式估算，只能靠线上压测才能得知
约 N×M，大多数读会命中缓存
options_en: Equal to a single host's memory M.
Equal to the database's total size.
Impossible to estimate with any formula; only production load testing can tell.
Roughly N times M; as long as it holds most recent posts, most reads hit the cache.
why: 分片式缓存容量随节点数线性增长（N×M）；结合读集中在近期帖子的模式，不大的集群就能挡住大部分读流量。
why_en: A sharded cache's capacity scales linearly with node count, roughly N times M, and since reads concentrate on recent posts, even a modest cluster absorbs most read traffic.
optionExplanations: 只按单台主机算，忽略了分片式缓存靠多台机器拼出总容量这件事。
缓存容量不需要等于数据库总大小，能装下大部分近期热数据就够。
总容量其实能直接用节点数和单机内存算出来，不需要靠压测猜。
对：分片式缓存总容量约等于 N×M，随节点数线性增长，配合读集中在近期的模式就能挡住大部分流量。
optionExplanations_en: Counting only one host's memory ignores that a sharded cache pools capacity across many machines.
Cache capacity doesn't need to match the database's total size — holding most of the hot recent data is enough.
The total capacity can actually be computed directly from node count and per-node memory, no load test needed to guess it.
Correct: a sharded cache's total capacity is roughly N times M, scaling linearly with node count, enough to absorb most traffic given how reads concentrate on recent posts.

q: 按 postId 分片的帖子缓存，还残留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains with a postId-sharded post cache?
options: 热 key 原样搬进缓存单点
缓存的成本高于数据库
TTL 无法与 LRU 共存
Redis 不支持按 key 分片
options_en: The hot-key problem gets copied straight into the cache: the shard holding a viral post gets crushed while other nodes sit underused.
The cache costs more than the database.
TTL and LRU can't coexist.
Redis doesn't support sharding by key.
why: 分片缓存里每个帖子只住一个节点，爆款的全部流量仍砸向单点，很多主机反而利用率低下。
why_en: In a sharded cache each post lives on exactly one node, so a viral post's entire traffic still slams a single node while the rest sit underused.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

optionExplanations: 对：分片路由把同一个 key 固定钉死在一个节点上，没有第二个节点能分担它的流量。
缓存的成本和这个问题无关，这里讨论的是热点分布，不是价格。
TTL 和 LRU 是两套独立机制，完全可以同时使用，互不冲突。
Redis 完全支持按 key 做一致性哈希分片，这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: shard routing pins a given key permanently to one node, and no second node exists to share that node's traffic.
Cache cost is unrelated to this problem — the issue here is hotspot distribution, not pricing.
TTL and LRU are two independent mechanisms that work together fine, with no conflict between them.
Redis fully supports consistent-hash sharding by key, so that claim just isn't true.
scenario: 帖子缓存按 postId 分片后容量够了，但一条爆款帖被百万人同时刷，单节点约 10 万 QPS 封顶。
scenario_en: After sharding the post cache by postId capacity is fine, but one viral post is read by a million people while a single node tops out near 100k QPS.

scenario: 单个爆款帖子的读流量超过任何一台缓存节点的能力上限，按 postId 分片没有出路。
scenario_en: A single viral post has more read traffic than any one cache node can serve, so postId-based sharding has no path forward.
q: 『great』级别的缓存架构是？
q_en: What is the 'great' cache architecture?
options: 在分片缓存前面再加一层缓存
复制式：任何实例都能服务任意帖子
给热分片换更大的机器
把爆款帖子内联进每个用户的 feed 条目
options_en: Add yet another cache layer in front of the sharded cache.
Switch to a replicated cache: every instance can serve any post, and the load balancer spreads requests across all N instances.
Upgrade the hot shard's node to a bigger machine.
Inline the viral post directly into every user's feed entry.
why: 从『每个帖子只住一个节点』改成『每个实例都可服务任何帖子』，热 key 吞吐直接乘 N，且无需任何协调。
why_en: Switching from 'each post lives on one node' to 'every instance can serve any post' multiplies hot-key throughput by N with zero coordination needed.
whenOtherWins: 没有极端热 key、但数据量大时，分片缓存能容纳多得多的不同帖子，总命中率更高。
tradeoff: 复制式的热 key 吞吐 vs 分片式的总容量

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个缓存实例都保存相同的完整数据副本，任何实例都能应答任意 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replicated cache keeps a full copy on every instance so any instance can answer any key.

optionExplanations: 在分片缓存前再叠一层缓存，热 key 还是集中砸向同一个分片，没解决单点问题。
对：所有实例保有相同的数据副本，负载均衡器可以把请求随意撒给任意一台，不用管哪台『拥有』这个帖子。
垂直扩容单个热分片的机器还是有硬件上限，撑不住持续增长的热度。
把爆款帖子内联进每个用户的 feed 条目，存储会随粉丝数线性膨胀，方向反了。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking another cache layer in front still funnels a hot key at the same single shard, leaving the core problem unsolved.
Correct: every instance holds an identical copy of the data, so the load balancer can route a request to any of them without caring which one 'owns' the post.
Vertically scaling the hot shard's machine still hits a hardware ceiling that can't outrun continued growth in popularity.
Inlining a viral post into every user's feed entry makes storage balloon with follower count, the wrong direction entirely.

q: 复制式缓存的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of a replicated cache?
options: 写扇出的整体写入量会因为复制而成倍地显著变大
读取延迟会因此显著上升
初期 miss 变多，最多 N 次回源
缓存条目将无法再设置 TTL
options_en: Write fan-out's total write volume grows several-fold because of the replication.
Read latency rises significantly because of it.
More initial misses: the same viral post may be fetched from the origin once per instance, N times instead of once.
Cache entries can no longer have a TTL set on them.
why: 每个实例独立回源，冷启动时同一帖子最多 N 次 miss；拿 N 次回源换 N 倍热 key 吞吐是划算的交换。
why_en: Each instance fetches from the origin independently, so a cold start can cost up to N misses for the same post, a fair trade for N times the hot-key throughput.
optionExplanations: 复制式缓存改变的是读路径的服务方式，跟写扇出的机制没有关系。
复制式缓存反而是为了降低热 key 的读延迟，说延迟上升和目的相反。
对：多个实例第一次遇到同一个帖子时各自单独去数据库要一次，这些 miss 并行发生、彼此独立。
复制式缓存照样能设 TTL，跟分片式没有区别，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: A replicated cache changes how reads are served, unrelated to the write-path fan-out mechanism.
A replicated cache exists specifically to cut hot-key read latency, so claiming latency rises is the opposite of the goal.
Correct: multiple instances each hit the database once on their own first encounter with the same post, and those misses happen independently in parallel.
A replicated cache can set a TTL just fine, no different from a sharded one, so that claim doesn't hold.
scenario: 为扛住爆款热 key，把热帖复制到每个缓存节点；集群冷启动后要评估这么做的代价。
scenario_en: To survive a viral hot key we replicate hot posts onto every cache node, and now we assess what that costs right after a cold start.

q: 分片缓存与复制缓存，在『单个热 key 的吞吐上限』维度上的区别是？
q_en: How do sharded and replicated caches differ on single-hot-key throughput?
options: 分片卡单点；复制乘 N 倍
两者的热 key 吞吐相同
复制式的热 key 吞吐更低
取决于 TTL 设多长
options_en: Sharded: hot-key throughput is roughly one node's limit; replicated: roughly N times one node's limit, with no coordination needed.
The two have identical hot-key throughput.
A replicated cache actually has lower hot-key throughput.
It depends entirely on how long the TTL is set.
why: 这是空间换吞吐：分片容量大但热 key 卡单点；复制容量小但热 key 吞吐乘 N。
why_en: This is capacity traded for throughput: sharding caps a hot key at one node, while replication multiplies hot-key throughput by N.
tradeoff: 热 key 吞吐 vs 总缓存容量
optionExplanations: 对：分片式里热 key 卡在单节点的上限；复制式里每个实例都能应答，吞吐乘 N 且不需要协调。
两者在热 key 这个维度上差得很远，说『相同』忽视了架构本质的不同。
把两者的能力关系说反了，复制式的热 key 吞吐其实更高，不是更低。
TTL 决定的是数据新鲜度，跟热 key 能被多少个节点同时服务是两个独立维度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: sharded caps a hot key at one node's limit, while replicated lets every instance answer, multiplying throughput by N with no coordination.
The two differ a lot on this dimension; calling them 'identical' ignores their fundamentally different architectures.
This reverses the actual relationship — a replicated cache's hot-key throughput is higher, not lower.
TTL governs data freshness, a separate dimension from how many nodes can serve a hot key at once.
scenario: 一条爆款帖被百万人同时刷，单个 Redis 节点约 10 万 QPS 封顶；要在分片和复制间选。
scenario_en: A viral post is hit by a million people at once and a single Redis node tops out near 100k QPS, so we choose between sharding and replication.

scenario: 用 Redis 缓存帖子：key 按 postId；帖子极少编辑所以 TTL 可以设 1 天；一旦编辑要立刻失效。
scenario_en: Use Redis to cache posts by postId. Posts are rarely edited, so TTL can be one day, but edits must invalidate immediately.
q: 哪组命令符合这套策略？
q_en: Which Redis command sequence matches this caching strategy?
options: SET post:p123 ... EX 60，一分钟就过期
SET post:p123 ...（完全不带 TTL），并在每次创建新帖时 DEL 对应 key
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400，编辑帖子时 DEL 对应 key
只用 GET post:p123，miss 时完全不做任何回填
options_en: SET post:p123 ... EX 60, expiring after one minute.
SET post:p123 ... with no TTL at all, and DEL the matching key whenever any new post is created.
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400, and DEL the matching key whenever the post is edited.
Only GET post:p123, doing absolutely no backfill at all on a miss.
codeSample:
# fill on miss, long TTL (1 day)
SET post:p123 '{"content":"..."}' EX 86400

# read path
GET post:p123

# post edited: precise invalidation
DEL post:p123
why: 长 TTL（EX 86400）匹配『帖子几乎不变』的事实，编辑时 DEL 精确失效；TTL 60 秒会造成大量无谓 miss。
why_en: A long TTL of EX 86400 matches how rarely posts change, while DEL on edit gives precise invalidation, unlike a 60-second TTL that would cause needless misses.
whenOtherWins: 若帖子频繁编辑且必须立刻可见，就该缩短 TTL 或改成写时同步更新缓存。
tradeoff: 长 TTL+精确失效 vs 短 TTL 的保守新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 60 秒的时长远短于帖子几乎不变的真实变化频率，会制造大量不必要的 miss。
在创建时机做失效没有意义，而且完全没有兜底的自动清理。
对：一天的时长匹配帖子极少变化的事实，编辑发生时精确删掉对应 key。
只读不写意味着缓存永远不会被填充，等于没有缓存。
optionExplanations_en: A 60-second span is far shorter than how rarely a post actually changes, causing needless misses.
Invalidating at creation time doesn't make sense, and there's no automatic cleanup as a backstop either.
Correct: a one-day span matches how rarely posts actually change, with a precise delete on that key the moment an edit happens.
Read-only with no write path means the cache never gets populated at all — effectively no cache.

q: 把『爆款帖子读扇出』的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the viral-post read fan-out decision chain in the right order.
steps: 代价：分片缓存自身也有热 key——爆款所在的分片照样被打爆
缓解：接受最多 N 次回源和更小的有效容量，DynamoDB 能吸收这点波动
需求：爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，而 DynamoDB 只有负载均匀才能高吞吐
升级：换成复制式缓存+负载均衡，任何实例都能服务任何帖子
选型：在 Post 表前加分布式缓存，长 TTL + LRU
why: 链条完整走一遍：热读需求 → 加缓存 → 缓存自己也热 → 复制式缓存摊平 → 接受少量回源。
why_en: The chain runs from a hot-read requirement, to adding a cache, to the cache itself getting hot, to replication spreading the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

q: 复制式缓存能装下的『不同帖子总数』比分片式少，为什么可以接受？
q_en: Why is it acceptable that a replicated cache holds fewer distinct posts than a sharded cache?
options: 因为帖子会自动压缩
因为可以无限加内存
因为旧帖子几乎根本没人会去读，不缓存它们也没什么影响
DynamoDB 兜得住这点额外 miss
options_en: Because posts get automatically compressed.
Because memory can be added without limit.
Because almost nobody ever reads old posts anyway, so not caching them makes no real difference.
Because the DynamoDB backend can absorb some read-throughput variability, and the small extra misses fall well within that.
why: 复制牺牲了有效容量，换来热 key 吞吐；落库的 miss 变多一点没关系，DynamoDB 不是不能读，只是不能被单点打爆。
why_en: Replication trades away effective capacity for hot-key throughput, and the extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed.
optionExplanations: 帖子并不会自动压缩，这是编出来的机制。
内存可以加但成本会跟着线性上涨，不是『无限』就没代价。
『旧帖子根本没人读』说得太绝对，只是读得少，不是完全没有。
对：复制牺牲的是有效容量，多出来的 miss 落回 DynamoDB 完全兜得住，不是被单点打爆。
optionExplanations_en: Posts don't actually get auto-compressed — that's a fabricated mechanism.
Memory can be added, but cost keeps scaling linearly with it; 'unlimited' doesn't mean free.
'Nobody reads old posts' overstates it — they're read less often, not never.
Correct: replication trades away effective capacity, and the resulting extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed, not a single-point overload.
scenario: 复制缓存把同一批热帖复制到每个节点，能缓存的不同帖子数因此变少；后端是 DynamoDB。
scenario_en: A replicated cache copies the same hot posts onto every node, so it holds fewer distinct posts, and DynamoDB sits behind it.

scenario: 45 分钟面试，你刚画完 naive feed（读时现查关注列表再逐个拉帖），自己清楚它扛不住大扇出，可分页、存储等需求都还没铺。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview you've just drawn the naive feed (query the follow list at read time, then pull each user's posts), you know it won't survive large fan-out, and pagination and storage are still unbuilt.
q: 面对这个明显不 scale 的 naive 方案，此刻最该怎么处理？
q_en: Facing this obviously non-scaling naive design, what's the right move right now?
options: 口头声明『我知道这版不 scale，先铺完再单独解决扩展』，然后继续铺其余需求
默默擦掉 naive 方案，直接重画一个能 scale 的最终设计，免得被看出方案不成熟
当场为方案不成熟道歉，坦白自己一时只能想到这么多
立刻停下把扇出优化到位，确认这块彻底没问题再回来做别的需求
options_en: Say out loud 'I know this won't scale; I'll lay it out first and fix scaling separately,' then keep covering the rest.
Quietly erase the naive design and redraw a scalable final version so the interviewer never sees anything unpolished.
Apologize on the spot for an immature design and admit this is all you can think of for now.
Stop immediately and perfect the fan-out until it's fully solved before returning to the other requirements.
why: 主动说『我知道这不 scale』证明你已识别瓶颈，比藏起来更得分；代价是白板上暂留一个已知不完善的方案，靠后半程补回来。
why_en: Announcing 'I know this won't scale' proves you already spotted the bottleneck and scores better than hiding it, at the cost of leaving a known-incomplete design on the board to fix later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次写或读要触发的下游操作数量；关注多则读扇出大，被关注多则写扇出大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is the number of downstream operations one read or write triggers; following many people means large read fan-out, being followed by many means large write fan-out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最直白但不考虑扩展的第一版设计，用来先铺通功能、之后再单独优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A naive solution is the simplest first-pass design that ignores scale, used to make the flow work before optimizing separately.

optionExplanations: 对：显式标注已识别瓶颈，再按广度优先把其余需求铺完，时间才够。
擦掉重画会让面试官看不到你识别问题的过程，反而丢掉『发现瓶颈』这一分。
道歉传递不自信，naive 起步是标准打法，不是需要致歉的失误。
还没铺完广度就深挖单点，正是最常见的失败模式，容易时间失控。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: flag the known bottleneck out loud, then keep covering breadth first so time holds up.
Erasing and redrawing hides your problem-spotting, costing you the 'found the bottleneck' credit.
Apologizing signals low confidence; a naive start is standard practice, not a mistake to atone for.
Deep-diving one spot before breadth is done is the classic failure mode and blows the clock.

scenario: 同样 45 分钟，你刚发现 naive feed 的扇出瓶颈，很想立刻把它优化到完美；可分页、follow、存储等需求都还空着。
scenario_en: Same 45 minutes: you've just found the naive feed's fan-out bottleneck and want to perfect it immediately, but pagination, follow, and storage are all still empty.
q: 如果现在一头扎进扇出细节、不先铺完广度，最可能的失败结局是？
q_en: If you dive straight into fan-out details before covering breadth, what's the most likely failure outcome?
options: 时间被这一处深挖吃光，收尾时多个功能需求仍无任何设计，面试官看到残缺系统
越深入越好，深度分永远压过广度分，所以提前扎进去其实稳赚不亏
面试官一定会及时喊停并把你拉回来，所以无论扎多深都能被纠正、根本不用自己控节奏
没先把数据模型定死就深挖，方案会因为缺少前置依赖而根本推进不下去
options_en: The clock gets eaten by that one deep dive, and at wrap-up several requirements still have no design, so the interviewer sees a half-built system.
Deeper is always better and depth points always beat breadth points, so diving in early is a sure win.
The interviewer will always stop you in time and pull you back, so any depth self-corrects and you never need to pace yourself.
Deep-diving before nailing the data model means the plan can't move forward for lack of prerequisites.
why: 广度没铺完就深挖，时间预算被单点吃光，收尾时多个需求还空着——而 mid/senior 的评分底线正是『完整且满足需求的高层设计』。
why_en: Deep-diving before breadth is done drains the time budget on one spot and leaves requirements empty at wrap-up, yet the passing bar for mid and senior is a complete high-level design that meets the requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个组件或瓶颈做深入的方案讨论，展开取舍与实现细节，而非停在高层框图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is an in-depth discussion of one component or bottleneck, working through trade-offs and implementation instead of staying at the high-level diagram.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把所有功能需求都对应到高层组件、先铺通整套系统的宽度，而非某一处的深度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Breadth means mapping every functional requirement to high-level components and covering the whole system's width before going deep anywhere.

optionExplanations: 对：时间是零和的，深挖吃掉预算就没有收尾，残缺系统直接触底评分线。
深度确实值钱，但缺了广度会连基础及格线都够不到，谈不上稳赚。
指望面试官救场是把节奏交给别人，控时是候选人自己的责任。
没有完整数据模型也能口头讨论扇出方向，这不是深挖失败的真正原因。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: time is zero-sum, and a deep dive that eats the budget leaves no wrap-up, hitting the floor of the score.
Depth is valuable, but missing breadth fails even the base bar, so it's no sure win.
Relying on the interviewer to rescue you hands over pacing, which is the candidate's own job.
You can discuss fan-out direction verbally without a full data model, so this isn't the real cause.

scenario: 你面的是 mid-level（E4）后端岗，45 分钟设计 News Feed；级别决定了这一轮的评分重心。
scenario_en: You're interviewing for a mid-level (E4) backend role, 45 minutes to design News Feed; the level sets what this round grades on.
q: E4 这一轮，面试官的评分方式和你的精力分配该是怎样？
q_en: At E4, how does the interviewer grade and how should you split your effort?
options: 广度为主（约 80/20），会逐个追问基础组件『它是做什么的』，但不指望你主动发现所有扩展瓶颈
深度为主（约 40/60），默认你懂基础，只想听你把复杂场景深挖透彻
广度深度各半，还要求你在毫无提示的情况下就主动暴露所有的性能瓶颈，并至少把其中两处深挖到底
只要画出组件框图就够，不必解释每个组件到底负责什么
options_en: Mostly breadth (about 80/20); they'll probe each basic component with 'what does it do?' but don't expect you to surface every scaling bottleneck yourself.
Mostly depth (about 40/60); they assume you know the basics and just want to hear you deep-dive the hard scenarios.
Half breadth half depth, and you must proactively expose every performance bottleneck fully unprompted and deep-dive at least two of them.
Just drawing the component boxes is enough; you don't need to explain what each component actually does.
why: E4 底线是『功能完整、满足需求的高层设计』，约 80% 广度；面试官不指望你自查瓶颈，会接手后半程并逐个盘问基础组件的作用。
why_en: The E4 bar is a functional high-level design that meets the requirements, roughly 80% breadth; the interviewer doesn't expect you to self-audit bottlenecks and will drive the later stages while probing each basic component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中级工程师职级；系统设计轮以广度为主，约 80% 广度 20% 深度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E4 is the mid-level engineer tier; its system-design round is breadth-first, about 80% breadth and 20% depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把功能需求映射成组件与数据流的整体框图，还未展开到深挖细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A high-level design maps functional requirements onto components and data flow as an overall diagram, before any deep-dive detail.

optionExplanations: 对：E4 求完整可用的高层设计，面试官会盘问基础组件并驱动后半程。
深度为主是 staff+ 的标准，E4 阶段不会这样压深度。
无提示暴露瓶颈并深挖两处，是 senior（E5）的要求，超出 E4 及格线。
面试官恰恰会追问每个组件的职责，画框图不解释会被判为只知其名。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: E4 wants a complete, functional high-level design; the interviewer probes basics and drives the back half.
Depth-first is the staff+ standard; E4 isn't pushed on depth like this.
Surfacing bottlenecks unprompted and deep-diving two is the senior (E5) bar, above E4.
The interviewer will in fact ask each component's role, so unexplained boxes read as name-only knowledge.

scenario: 同一道 News Feed，这次面的是 senior（E5）后端岗，还是 45 分钟；级别抬高改变了及格线。
scenario_en: Same News Feed, this time for a senior (E5) backend role, still 45 minutes; the higher level moves the passing bar.
q: 相比 E4，E5 把这道题的及格线抬到了哪里？
q_en: Compared with E4, where does E5 raise the passing bar on this question?
options: 约 60/40 广度深度：快速掠过高层设计，主动（不靠提示）点出扇出瓶颈，并至少深挖两个 deep dive
和 E4 一样 80/20，只是要求组件图画得更工整、命名更规范一些
纯深度 40/60，面试官全程只在真正需要聚焦时才短暂介入，期待你完全独立地发现、预防并解决一切潜在问题
只要能背出扇出读、扇出写两种策略的定义，不必落到本题具体怎么用
options_en: About 60/40 breadth to depth: speed through the high-level design, proactively (unprompted) name the fan-out bottleneck, and deep-dive at least two areas.
Same 80/20 as E4, just with a tidier component diagram and more standardized naming.
Pure depth at 40/60, with the interviewer briefly stepping in only to focus, expecting you to fully independently find and prevent every potential issue.
Just reciting the definitions of fan-out-on-read and fan-out-on-write is enough, without applying them to this problem.
why: E5 要证明有 hands-on 深度：因此快速铺完广度、主动暴露扇出瓶颈，并挑至少两处深挖到能讲清 pros/cons；代价是广度必须提速。
why_en: E5 must show hands-on depth, so you cover breadth fast, proactively surface the fan-out bottleneck, and deep-dive at least two areas enough to explain the pros and cons, at the cost of speeding up breadth to free time for depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高级工程师职级；系统设计轮约 60% 广度 40% 深度，需主动暴露瓶颈并深挖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is the senior engineer tier; its system-design round is about 60% breadth and 40% depth, requiring you to surface bottlenecks proactively and deep-dive.

termDefinitions.term: 扇出读/扇出写 / fan-out on read vs write
termDefinitions.meaning: 读时现查合并各账号的帖子叫扇出读；发帖时预先写进每个粉丝的 feed 叫扇出写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read merges each account's posts at read time; fan-out on write pushes a new post into every follower's feed when it's created.

optionExplanations: 对：E5 要主动暴露扇出并深挖至少两处，快速走完广度以腾出深度时间。
只把图画整齐仍停在 E4 的广度水平，够不到 E5 对深度的要求。
只在聚焦时介入、独立预防一切，是 staff+ 的标准，比 E5 更高。
背定义而不落到本题，正是 E5 面试官想淘汰的『纸上谈兵』。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: E5 must proactively surface fan-out and deep-dive at least two, racing through breadth to free depth time.
A tidier diagram still sits at E4's breadth level and misses E5's depth requirement.
Intervening only to focus and preventing everything independently is the staff+ standard, above E5.
Reciting definitions without applying them is exactly the paper-only answer E5 interviewers screen out.
